title.zh: 卷一百十一 志第六十四 禮十四
title.raw: 卷一百十一 志第六十四 禮十四 Volume 111 Treatises 64: Rites 14

sentences.zh: 禮十四

translations.literal: Rites Fourteen
translations.idiomatic: Rites 14

sentences.zh: 〈（嘉禮二）〉

translations.literal: (Auspicious Rites Two)
translations.idiomatic: (Auspicious Ceremonies, Part Two)

sentences.zh: ○冊立皇后儀冊命皇太子儀冊皇太子妃儀公主受封儀冊命親王大臣儀

translations.literal: ○ Ceremonies for installing the empress; ceremonies for investing the crown prince by patent; ceremonies for investing the crown prince's consort; ceremonies for a princess receiving ennoblement; ceremonies for investing princes and great ministers by patent
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonies for installing the empress; for investing the crown prince; for investing the crown prince's consort; for ennobling a princess; and for investing princes and great ministers

sentences.zh: 冊立皇后。

translations.literal: Installing the empress.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony for installing the empress.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年，立琅邪郡夫人王氏為皇后，命所司擇日備禮冊命。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianlong, Lady Wang, Lady of Langye Commandery, was established as empress; the relevant offices were ordered to select a day and prepare the ritual of investiture by patent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianlong (960), Lady Wang of Langye Commandery was installed as empress, and the responsible offices were instructed to choose a date and prepare the full patent ceremony.

sentences.zh: 自後，凡制書云「冊命」者，多不行冊禮。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever an edict said "investiture by patent," for the most part the patent ceremony was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, whenever an edict spoke of "investiture by patent," the formal patent ceremony was usually omitted.

sentences.zh: 後妃皆寫冊命告身，以金花龍鳳羅紙、金塗褾袋，有司進入，學士院草制，宣於正殿。

translations.literal: Consorts all had written patents of investiture and appointment credentials, using gold-flowered dragon-phoenix gauze paper and gold-gilded fitted cases; the relevant offices submitted them, the Hanlin Academy drafted the text, and it was proclaimed in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts received written patents and appointment credentials on gold-flowered dragon-phoenix gauze, in gold-gilded cases; the appropriate offices forwarded them, the Hanlin Academy drafted the text, and it was proclaimed in the main audience hall.

sentences.zh: 近臣、牧守、宗室皆修貢禮，群臣拜表稱賀，又詣內東門奉箋賀皇后。

translations.literal: Close ministers, prefects, and members of the imperial clan all performed tribute rites; the officials submitted memorials of congratulation, and also went to the Inner Eastern Gate to present congratulatory documents to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Close advisers, regional governors, and imperial clansmen all offered tribute; the officials submitted congratulatory memorials, and also went to the Inner Eastern Gate to present congratulatory documents to the empress.

sentences.zh: 真宗冊德妃劉氏為皇后，不欲令藩臣貢賀，不降制於外廷，止命學士草詞付中書。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong invested Virtuous Consort Liu as empress; he did not wish to have frontier officials offer tribute congratulations, did not issue an edict to the outer court, and only ordered academicians to draft the text and deliver it to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong invested Virtuous Consort Liu as empress, he did not want frontier officials to offer congratulatory tribute, issued no edict to the outer court, and merely had Hanlin academicians draft the text and pass it to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仁宗冊皇后曹氏，其冊制如皇太子，玉用瑉玉五十簡，匣依冊之長短；

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong invested Empress Cao, her patent followed that of the crown prince: jade used min-jade in fifty slips; the case followed the length of the patent;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong invested Empress Cao, her patent followed the crown prince's model: fifty slips of min-jade, with a case sized to the patent's length;

sentences.zh: 寶用金，方一寸五分，高一寸，其文曰“皇后之寶”，盤螭紐，綬並緣冊寶法物約舊制為之，匣、盝並朱漆金塗銀裝。

translations.literal: The seal used gold, one inch five fen square, one inch high; its inscription read "Seal of the Empress," with a coiled-chi knob; the cord and border regalia for the patent and seal approximated the old regulations; case and box were both cinnabar lacquer with gold-gilded silver fittings.
translations.idiomatic: the seal was of gold, one and a half inches square and one inch high, inscribed "Seal of the Empress," with a coiled-dragon knob; cords and accompanying regalia for the patent and seal followed the old regulations in broad outline; case and casket were both cinnabar lacquer with gold-gilded silver mountings.

sentences.zh: 其禮與《通禮》異，不立仗，不設縣。

translations.literal: Its ritual differed from the Comprehensive Rites: no guard of honor was posted, and no suspended bells were set up.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony differed from the Comprehensive Rites: no guard of honor was posted and no ritual music was arranged.

sentences.zh: 前一日，守宮設次於朝堂，設冊寶使、副次於東門外，命婦次於受冊寶殿門外，設皇后受冊寶位於殿庭階下北向。

translations.literal: On the previous day, the palace attendants set up a pavilion in the audience hall; set up pavilions for the patent-and-seal envoy and deputy outside the eastern gate; titled ladies' pavilions outside the gate of the hall for receiving the patent and seal; and set the empress's place for receiving the patent and seal on the steps below the hall courtyard, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the ceremony, palace attendants set up pavilions in the audience hall; pavilions for the patent-and-seal envoy and deputy outside the eastern gate; titled ladies' pavilions outside the hall where the patent and seal would be received; and the empress's receiving station on the steps below the hall courtyard, facing north.

sentences.zh: 奉禮設冊寶使位於內東門外，副使、內侍位於其南，差退，東向北上，冊寶案位於使前南向，又設內給事位於北廂南向。

translations.literal: Ceremonial attendants set the patent-and-seal envoy's place outside the Inner Eastern Gate; the deputy envoy and inner attendants' places south of it, somewhat withdrawn, facing east from the north; the patent-and-seal table south of and before the envoy; and also set the inner chamberlain's place in the north wing, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial attendants placed the envoy's station outside the Inner Eastern Gate, with the deputy and inner attendants to the south, slightly withdrawn, facing east from the north; the patent-and-seal table before the envoy, facing south; and the inner chamberlain's station in the north wing, facing south.

sentences.zh: 其日，百官常服早入次，禮直官、通事舍人先引中書令、侍中、門下侍郎、中書侍郎及奉冊寶官，執事人絳衣介幘，詣垂拱殿門就次，以俟冊降。

translations.literal: On that day, all officials in regular dress entered their pavilions early; ritual officers and communication chamberlains first led the Secretariat Director, Attendant-in-Chief, Vice Director of the Chancellery, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and patent-and-seal bearers; attendants in crimson robes and kerchiefs, proceeding to the Chui'gong Hall gate to take their places, awaiting the descent of the patent.
translations.idiomatic: On the day itself, all officials in regular dress entered their stations early; ritual officers and communication chamberlains first led the Secretariat Director, Attendant-in-Chief, Chancellery and Secretariat vice directors, and patent-and-seal bearers, with attendants in crimson robes and caps, to the Chui'gong Hall gate to wait for the patent to be brought down.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、通事舍人分引宰臣、樞密、冊寶使副、百官詣文德殿立班，東西相向。

translations.literal: Ritual officers and communication chamberlains separately led the chief ministers, Privy Council members, patent-and-seal envoy and deputy, and all officials to the Wende Hall to form ranks, facing each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers and communication chamberlains then led the chief ministers, Privy Council members, the patent-and-seal envoy and deputy, and all officials to the Wende Hall to form ranks facing each other east and west.

sentences.zh: 內侍二員自內承旨降皇后冊寶出垂拱殿，奉冊寶官俱搢笏率執事人，禮直官導中書侍郎押冊，中書令後從，門下侍郎押寶，侍中後從，由東上閣門出，至文德殿庭權置。

translations.literal: Two inner attendants, receiving the order from within, brought down the empress's patent and seal from the Chui'gong Hall; all patent-and-seal bearers inserted their tablets and led attendants; ritual officers guided the Secretariat Vice Director escorting the patent, the Secretariat Director following behind, the Chancellery Vice Director escorting the seal, the Attendant-in-Chief following behind; they exited through the Upper Eastern Gate, and temporarily placed them in the Wende Hall courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Two inner attendants, acting on orders from within, brought the empress's patent and seal down from the Chui'gong Hall; the patent-and-seal bearers all inserted their tablets and led their attendants; ritual officers guided the Secretariat Vice Director escorting the patent with the Secretariat Director behind, and the Chancellery Vice Director escorting the seal with the Attendant-in-Chief behind; they exited through the Upper Eastern Gate and temporarily set them down in the Wende Hall courtyard.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、通事舍人引使、副就位，次引侍中於使前，西向稱“有制”，典儀曰“再拜”，讚者承傳，使、副、在位官皆再拜，宣曰：“贈尚書令、冀王曹彬孫女冊為皇后，命公等持節展禮。”

translations.literal: Ritual officers and communication chamberlains led the envoy and deputy to their places; next led the Attendant-in-Chief before the envoy, facing west and announcing "There is an edict"; the master of ceremonies said "Bow twice"; the announcer transmitted it; the envoy, deputy, and officials in attendance all bowed twice; the proclamation read: "The granddaughter of the posthumously titled Secretariat Director and Prince of Ji, Cao Bin, is invested as empress; We command you to hold the staff of authority and perform the ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers and communication chamberlains led the envoy and deputy to their stations, then led the Attendant-in-Chief before the envoy, who faced west and announced, "There is an edict." The master of ceremonies called for a double bow; the announcer relayed the command, and the envoy, deputy, and all present officials bowed twice. The proclamation ran: "The granddaughter of the late Secretariat Director and Prince of Ji, Cao Bin, is invested as empress. We command you to bear the staff of authority and conduct the ceremony."

sentences.zh: 使、副再拜，侍中還位，門下侍郎帥主節者詣使東北，主節以節授門下侍郎，門下侍郎執節授冊使，冊使跪受，興，付主節，幡隨節立於使左。

translations.literal: The envoy and deputy bowed twice; the Attendant-in-Chief returned to his place; the Chancellery Vice Director led the staff-bearer to the envoy's northeast; the staff-bearer handed the staff to the Chancellery Vice Director; the Chancellery Vice Director, holding the staff, handed it to the patent envoy; the patent envoy knelt to receive it, rose, and handed it to the staff-bearer; the banner followed the staff and stood to the envoy's left.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy and deputy bowed again; the Attendant-in-Chief returned to his place; the Chancellery Vice Director led the staff-bearer to the envoy's northeast; the staff was passed to the Chancellery Vice Director, who handed it to the patent envoy; the envoy knelt to receive it, rose, and returned it to the staff-bearer; the banner followed the staff and stood to the envoy's left.

sentences.zh: 次引中書令、侍中詣冊寶東北，西向立，中書侍郎引冊案立於中書令右，中書令取冊授冊寶使，使跪受，興，置於案，中書令、中書侍郎退復班。

translations.literal: Next they led the Secretariat Director and Attendant-in-Chief to the northeast of the patent and seal, standing facing west; the Secretariat Vice Director led the patent table to stand at the Secretariat Director's right; the Secretariat Director took the patent and handed it to the patent-and-seal envoy; the envoy knelt to receive it, rose, and placed it on the table; the Secretariat Director and Vice Director withdrew and returned to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Next the Secretariat Director and Attendant-in-Chief were led to the northeast of the patent and seal and stood facing west; the Secretariat Vice Director brought the patent table to the Director's right; the Director took the patent and handed it to the patent-and-seal envoy, who knelt to receive it, rose, and set it on the table; the Director and Vice Director withdrew to their ranks.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎引寶案於侍中之右，取寶授冊寶使如上儀，退復位，典儀讚拜訖，禮直官、通事舍人引使、副押冊寶，持節者前導，奉冊寶官奉舁，援衛如式，以次出朝堂門，詣內東門附內臣入進。

translations.literal: The Chancellery Vice Director led the seal table to the Attendant-in-Chief's right, took the seal and handed it to the patent-and-seal envoy by the same procedure, withdrew and returned to place; when the master of ceremonies had finished announcing the bows, ritual officers and communication chamberlains led the envoy and deputy escorting the patent and seal; the staff-bearer went before as guide; patent-and-seal bearers bore them aloft; escorts and guards as prescribed; in order they exited the audience hall gate, proceeded to the Inner Eastern Gate, and attached to inner attendants to enter and present.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery Vice Director brought the seal table to the Attendant-in-Chief's right and handed the seal to the envoy by the same procedure, then withdrew. When the bowing announcements were complete, ritual officers led the envoy and deputy escorting the patent and seal, with the staff-bearer going before, the bearers carrying them aloft, and guards as prescribed; they left in order through the audience hall gate, went to the Inner Eastern Gate, and were handed to inner attendants to enter and present.

sentences.zh: 內臣引內外命婦入就位，內侍詣閣請皇后服禕衣。

translations.literal: Inner attendants led inner and outer titled ladies to enter and take their places; inner attendants went to the pavilion to request that the empress don her ceremonial robe.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants led titled ladies from within and without to their stations; inner attendants went to the empress's quarters to ask her to don her ceremonial robe.

sentences.zh: 冊寶至，使、副俱東向內給事前，北內跪稱：“冊寶使李迪、副使王隨奉制授皇后冊寶。”

translations.literal: When the patent and seal arrived, the envoy and deputy both faced east before the inner chamberlain, knelt within the northern inner quarters and announced: "Patent-and-seal Envoy Li Di and Deputy Envoy Wang Sui, by imperial command, present the empress's patent and seal."
translations.idiomatic: When the patent and seal arrived, the envoy and deputy both faced east before the inner chamberlain and, kneeling within the inner palace, announced: "Patent-and-seal Envoy Li Di and Deputy Envoy Wang Sui, by imperial command, present the empress's patent and seal."

sentences.zh: 俯伏，興，退復位。

translations.literal: They bowed prostrate, rose, withdrew and returned to their places.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed prostrate, rose, and returned to their stations.

sentences.zh: 內給事入詣受冊寶殿門皇后前跪奏訖，內侍進詣使前，西面跪受冊寶，以授內謁者監，使退復位。

translations.literal: The inner chamberlain entered, went to the gate of the hall for receiving the patent and seal, knelt before the empress and reported; when finished, inner attendants advanced to before the envoy, knelt facing west to receive the patent and seal, and handed them to the Supervisor of Inner Chamberlains; the envoy withdrew and returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: The inner chamberlain entered, went to the hall gate, knelt before the empress and reported; when he had finished, inner attendants advanced to the envoy, knelt facing west to receive the patent and seal, and handed them to the Supervisor of Inner Chamberlains; the envoy withdrew to his station.

sentences.zh: 內謁者監、主當內臣持冊寶入內東門，內侍從之，以次入詣殿庭。

translations.literal: The Supervisor of Inner Chamberlains and duty inner attendants, holding the patent and seal, entered the Inner Eastern Gate; inner attendants followed; in order they entered and proceeded to the hall courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The Supervisor of Inner Chamberlains and duty attendants carried the patent and seal through the Inner Eastern Gate, followed by inner attendants, and entered the hall courtyard in order.

sentences.zh: 內侍讚引皇后降立庭中北向位，內侍跪取冊，次內侍跪取寶，興，立皇后右少前，西向，內侍二員進立皇后左少前東向，內侍稱“有制”，內侍讚皇后再拜，內侍奉冊進授皇后，皇后受以授內侍，次內侍奉寶亦然。

translations.literal: Inner attendants announced and led the empress down to stand at the north-facing place in the courtyard; an inner attendant knelt and took the patent; next an inner attendant knelt and took the seal, rose, and stood slightly before the empress's right, facing west; two inner attendants advanced and stood slightly before the empress's left, facing east; an inner attendant announced "There is an edict"; an inner attendant announced that the empress should bow twice; inner attendants, holding the patent, advanced and presented it to the empress; the empress received it and handed it to an inner attendant; next inner attendants presented the seal in the same manner.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants announced and led the empress down to her north-facing station in the courtyard; one attendant knelt and took the patent, then another knelt and took the seal, rose, and stood slightly before the empress's right, facing west; two attendants stood slightly before her left, facing east; an attendant announced, "There is an edict," and called for the empress to bow twice; attendants presented the patent, which the empress received and handed back to an attendant; the seal was presented in the same way.

sentences.zh: 復讚再拜訖，導皇后升坐，內臣引內外命婦稱賀如常儀。

translations.literal: Again they announced the double bow; when finished, they led the empress up to take her seat; inner attendants led inner and outer titled ladies to offer congratulations according to regular ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: After the second double bow, they led the empress to her seat; inner attendants led titled ladies from within and without to offer congratulations according to the usual rites.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，內侍導皇后降坐還閣，內外命婦班退。

translations.literal: When the ritual was complete, inner attendants led the empress down from her seat and back to her pavilion; inner and outer titled ladies withdrew in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, inner attendants led the empress from her seat back to her quarters; titled ladies from within and without withdrew in ranks.

sentences.zh: 皇后易常服，謝皇帝、皇太后，用常禮。

translations.literal: The empress changed into regular dress and thanked the emperor and empress dowager, using regular ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The empress changed into ordinary dress and thanked the emperor and empress dowager according to the usual rites.

sentences.zh: 百官詣東上閣門表賀。

translations.literal: All officials went to the Upper Eastern Gate to submit congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: All officials went to the Upper Eastern Gate to submit memorials of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 元祐五年八月，太皇太后詔：以皇帝納後，令翰林學士、御史中丞、兩省與太常禮官檢詳古今六禮沿革，參考《通禮》典故，具為成式。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year of Yuanyou, the Empress Dowager decreed: Because the emperor was taking an empress, she ordered Hanlin academicians, the Censor-in-Chief, both secretariats, and Director of Rites officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to examine in detail the evolution of the Six Rites ancient and modern, consult the precedents of the Comprehensive Rites, and compile them into a fixed form.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifth year of Yuanyou (1090), the Grand Empress Dowager decreed that, because the emperor was taking an empress, Hanlin academicians, the Censor-in-Chief, both secretariats, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices ritual officers should examine the evolution of the Six Rites through history, consult the Comprehensive Rites, and compile a definitive procedure.

sentences.zh: 群臣又議勘昏，御史中丞鄭雍等請不用陰陽之說，呂大防亦言不可，太后納之。

translations.literal: The officials also discussed divining the wedding date; Censor-in-Chief Zheng Yong and others requested not to use yin-yang doctrine; Lü Dagong also said it should not be done; the empress dowager accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The officials also debated divining the wedding date; Censor-in-Chief Zheng Yong and others asked that yin-yang calculations not be used; Lü Dagong likewise objected; the empress dowager accepted their view.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，三省、樞密院言：“六禮，命使納采、問名、納吉、納成、告期，差執政官攝太尉充使，侍從官或判宗正官攝宗正卿充副使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year, the Three Departments and Privy Council reported: "For the Six Rites—appointing envoys for presenting gifts, inquiring the name, presenting auspicious omens, presenting the bride-price, and announcing the date—dispatch chief councillors to act as Grand Marshal and serve as envoy; attendant officials or the official in charge of the Imperial Clan Court to act as Director of the Imperial Clan Court and serve as deputy envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixth year (1091), the Three Departments and Privy Council reported: "For the Six Rites—envoys for presenting gifts, inquiring the name, presenting auspicious omens, presenting the bride-price, and announcing the date—chief councillors should serve as acting Grand Marshal and envoy; attendant officials or the official in charge of the Imperial Clan Court should serve as acting Director of the Imperial Clan Court and deputy envoy.

sentences.zh: 以舊尚書省權為皇后行第。

translations.literal: Use the old Secretariat compound provisionally as the empress's family residence.
translations.idiomatic: The former Secretariat compound was to serve provisionally as the empress's family residence.

sentences.zh: 納采、問名同日，次日納吉、納成、告期。

translations.literal: Presenting gifts and inquiring the name on the same day; the next day presenting auspicious omens, presenting the bride-price, and announcing the date.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting gifts and inquiring the name would occur on the same day; presenting auspicious omens, the bride-price, and announcing the date would follow the next day.

sentences.zh: 納成用穀圭為贄，不用雁。

translations.literal: For presenting the bride-price use a grain jade tablet as the gift; do not use wild geese.
translations.idiomatic: For presenting the bride-price, a grain jade tablet would serve as the gift in place of wild geese.

sentences.zh: ‘請期’依《開寶禮》改為‘告期’，‘親迎’為‘命使奉迎’。

translations.literal: 'Requesting the date' according to the Kaibao Rites was changed to 'announcing the date'; 'the groom in person welcomes the bride' became 'appointing an envoy to conduct the welcome.'
translations.idiomatic: "Requesting the date," per the Kaibao Rites, was changed to "announcing the date"; "the groom welcomes the bride in person" became "appointing an envoy to conduct the welcome."

sentences.zh: 納采前，擇日告天地、宗廟。

translations.literal: Before presenting gifts, select a day to report to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: Before presenting gifts, a day would be chosen to report to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 皇帝臨軒發冊，同日，先遣冊禮使、副，次遣奉迎使，令文武百官詣行第班迎。”

translations.literal: The emperor would appear at the imperial audience to issue the patent; on the same day, first dispatch the patent-ceremony envoy and deputy; next dispatch the welcome envoy; order civil and military officials to proceed to the family residence and form ranks to welcome."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would appear at court to issue the patent; on the same day, the patent-ceremony envoy and deputy would be sent first, then the welcome envoy; civil and military officials would proceed to the family residence to form ranks of welcome."

sentences.zh: 又言：“據《開元禮》，納采、問名合用一使，納吉、納成各別日遣使。

translations.literal: They also said: "According to the Kaiyuan Rites, presenting gifts and inquiring the name should use one envoy together; presenting auspicious omens and presenting the bride-price each dispatch envoys on separate days.
translations.idiomatic: They added: "According to the Kaiyuan Rites, presenting gifts and inquiring the name should share one envoy, while presenting auspicious omens and the bride-price each require envoys on separate days.

sentences.zh: 今未委三禮共遣一使，或各遣使。

translations.literal: Now it is not decided whether the three rites should jointly dispatch one envoy, or each dispatch envoys.
translations.idiomatic: It was not yet decided whether the three later rites should share one envoy or each have its own.

sentences.zh: 又合依發冊例立仗。”

translations.literal: Also, it should follow the precedent for issuing the patent in posting the guard of honor."
translations.idiomatic: They also asked whether a guard of honor should be posted as when issuing a patent."

sentences.zh: 詔：“各遣使，文德殿發制依發冊立仗。”

translations.literal: An edict said: "Each dispatch envoys; issuing the edict at the Wende Hall shall follow the precedent for issuing the patent, with a guard of honor posted."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Each rite shall have its own envoy; issuing the edict at the Wende Hall shall follow the precedent for issuing the patent, with a guard of honor posted."

sentences.zh: 七年正月，詔尚書左丞蘇頌撰冊文並書。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, an edict ordered Secretariat Left Vice Director Su Song to draft and write the patent text.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year (1092), the court ordered Secretariat Left Vice Director Su Song to draft and write the patent text.

sentences.zh: 學士院上六禮辭語，其納采制文略曰：“太皇太后曰：「谘某官封姓名，渾元資始，肇經人倫，爰及夫婦，以奉天地、宗廟、社稷。

translations.literal: The Hanlin Academy submitted the wording for the Six Rites; the text for presenting gifts read in summary: "The Grand Empress Dowager says: 'Having consulted [title, name, and rank], from the origin of the cosmos, establishing human relations, extending to husband and wife, to serve Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin Academy submitted the formulas for the Six Rites. The edict for presenting gifts read in summary: "The Grand Empress Dowager says: 'Having consulted [title, name, and rank]—from the origin of the cosmos through the founding of human relations, down to the bond of husband and wife, to serve Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain—

sentences.zh: 謀於公卿，鹹以為宜。

translations.literal: Consulting the dukes and ministers, all considered it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: after consulting the chief ministers, all judged it fitting.

sentences.zh: 率由舊典，今遣使持節太尉某、宗正卿某以禮納采。」”

translations.literal: Following the old canon, We now dispatch envoys holding the staff of authority, Grand Marshal [name] and Director of the Imperial Clan Court [name], to present gifts according to ritual.'"
translations.idiomatic: Following the ancient canon, We now dispatch envoys bearing the staff of authority—Grand Marshal [name] and Director of the Imperial Clan Court [name]—to present gifts according to ritual.'"

sentences.zh: 其答文曰：“太皇太后嘉命，訪婚陋族，備數采擇，臣之女未閑教訓，衣履若而人。

translations.literal: The response read: "The Grand Empress Dowager's gracious command, seeking marriage with our humble clan, making us one of those selected; my daughter has not yet been fully instructed in deportment; her dress and conduct are as follows.
translations.idiomatic: The response read: "The Grand Empress Dowager's gracious command, seeking marriage with our humble clan and numbering us among those selected—my daughter has not yet been fully trained in deportment; her dress and conduct are as follows.

sentences.zh: 欽承舊章，肅奉典制。

translations.literal: Reverently accepting the old regulations, solemnly following the canonical procedure.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently accepting the ancient regulations, I solemnly follow the canonical procedure.

sentences.zh: 某官封糞土臣姓某稽首再拜承制詔。”

translations.literal: [Title and rank], this worthless subject [surname], kowtowing and bowing twice, receives the edict by imperial command."
translations.idiomatic: [Title and rank], this unworthy subject [surname], kowtowing and bowing twice, receives the edict by imperial command."

sentences.zh: 問名制曰：“兩儀合德，萬物之統，以聽內治，必谘令族。

translations.literal: The edict for inquiring the name read: "The two principles unite in virtue, the governing principle of the myriad things; to attend to inner governance, one must consult an eminent clan.
translations.idiomatic: The edict for inquiring the name read: "The two principles unite in virtue—the governing order of all things; to attend to inner governance, one must consult an eminent clan.

sentences.zh: 重宣舊典，今遣使持節某官以禮問名。”

translations.literal: Reiterating the old canon, We now dispatch an envoy holding the staff of authority, [official], to inquire the name according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Reiterating the ancient canon, We now dispatch an envoy bearing the staff of authority—[official]—to inquire the name according to ritual."

sentences.zh: 答曰：“使者重宣中制，問臣名族。

translations.literal: The response read: "The envoy has again proclaimed the central edict, inquiring as to my clan name.
translations.idiomatic: The response read: "The envoy has again proclaimed the central edict, inquiring as to my clan and lineage.

sentences.zh: 臣女，夫婦所生，先臣故某官之遺微孫，先臣故某官之遺曾孫，先臣故某官之遺孫，先臣故某官之外孫女，年若干。

translations.literal: My daughter, born of husband and wife, the surviving minor grandson of my late father, former [official]; the surviving great-grandson of my late father, former [official]; the surviving grandson of my late father, former [official]; the granddaughter by a daughter of my late father, former [official]; age [number].
translations.idiomatic: My daughter, born of my wife and me, is the surviving minor grandson of my late father, the former [official]; the surviving great-grandson of my late father, the former [official]; the surviving grandson of my late father, the former [official]; and the granddaughter by a daughter of my late father, the former [official]; she is [number] years of age.

sentences.zh: 欽承舊章，肅奉典制。”

translations.literal: Reverently accepting the old regulations, solemnly following the canonical procedure."
translations.idiomatic: Reverently accepting the ancient regulations, I solemnly follow the canonical procedure."

sentences.zh: 納吉制曰：“人謀龜筮，同符元吉，恭順典禮，今使某官以禮納吉。”

translations.literal: The edict for presenting auspicious omens read: "Human counsel and tortoise and milfoil divination alike accord with supreme good fortune; reverently following the canonical rites, We now send [official] to present auspicious omens according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The edict for presenting auspicious omens read: "Human counsel and tortoise and milfoil divination alike accord with supreme good fortune; reverently following the canonical rites, We now send [official] to present auspicious omens according to ritual."

sentences.zh: 答曰：“使者重宣中制，臣陋族卑鄙，憂懼不堪。

translations.literal: The response read: "The envoy has again proclaimed the central edict; my humble clan is base and lowly; I am overwhelmed with anxiety and fear.
translations.idiomatic: The response read: "The envoy has again proclaimed the central edict; my humble clan is base and unworthy; I am overwhelmed with anxiety and fear.

sentences.zh: 欽承舊章，肅奉典制。”

translations.literal: Reverently accepting the old regulations, solemnly following the canonical procedure."
translations.idiomatic: Reverently accepting the ancient regulations, I solemnly follow the canonical procedure."

sentences.zh: 納成制曰：“谘某官某之女，孝友恭儉，實維母儀，宜奉宗廟，永承天祚。

translations.literal: The edict for presenting the bride-price read: "Having consulted [official]'s daughter—filial, friendly, respectful, and frugal, truly a model of motherhood—fit to serve the ancestral temples and forever receive Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The edict for presenting the bride-price read: "Having consulted [official]'s daughter—filial, friendly, respectful, and frugal, truly a model of womanly virtue—fit to serve the ancestral temples and forever receive Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 以黝纁、穀圭、六馬以章典禮，今使某官以禮納成。”

translations.literal: With dark and light red silk, a grain jade tablet, and six horses to display the canonical rites, We now send [official] to present the bride-price according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: With dark and light red silk, a grain jade tablet, and six horses to display the canonical rites, We now send [official] to present the bride-price according to ritual."

sentences.zh: 答曰：“使者重宣中制，降婚卑陋，崇以上公，寵以豐禮，備物典策。

translations.literal: The response read: "The envoy has again proclaimed the central edict; bestowing marriage on our base and humble [house], honoring us with the rank of chief duke, favoring us with abundant rites, and providing the full regalia of canonical documents.
translations.idiomatic: The response read: "The envoy has again proclaimed the central edict; bestowing marriage on our base and humble house, honoring us with the rank of chief duke, favoring us with abundant rites, and providing the full regalia of canonical documents.

sentences.zh: 欽承舊章，肅奉典制。”

translations.literal: Reverently accepting the old regulations, solemnly following the canonical procedure."
translations.idiomatic: Reverently accepting the ancient regulations, I solemnly follow the canonical procedure."

sentences.zh: 告期制曰：“謀於公卿，大筮元龜，罔有不臧，吉日惟某月、某甲子可迎。

translations.literal: The edict for announcing the date read: "Consulting the dukes and ministers, divining with the great tortoise, nothing inauspicious; the auspicious day is the [cyclical day] of the [month].
translations.idiomatic: The edict for announcing the date read: "After consulting the chief ministers and divining with the great tortoise, nothing inauspicious was found; the auspicious day is the [cyclical day] of the [month], when the welcome may proceed.

sentences.zh: 率遵典禮，今遣某官以禮告期。”

translations.literal: Following the canonical rites, We now dispatch [official] to announce the date according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Following the canonical rites, We now dispatch [official] to announce the date according to ritual."

sentences.zh: 答曰：“使者重宣中制，以某月、某甲子吉日告期。

translations.literal: The response read: "The envoy has again proclaimed the central edict, announcing the date on the auspicious [cyclical day] of [month].
translations.idiomatic: The response read: "The envoy has again proclaimed the central edict, announcing that the auspicious [cyclical day] of [month] is the date for the welcome.

sentences.zh: 臣欽承舊章，肅奉典制。”

translations.literal: Your subject reverently accepts the old regulations, solemnly following the canonical procedure."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject reverently accepts the ancient regulations and solemnly follows the canonical procedure."

sentences.zh: 奉迎制曰：“禮之大體，欽順重正，其期維吉，典圖是若，今遣某官以禮奉迎。”

translations.literal: The edict for conducting the welcome read: "The great substance of ritual is reverent compliance with weighty rectitude; the date is auspicious; the canonical pattern is thus; We now dispatch [official] to conduct the welcome according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The edict for conducting the welcome read: "The great substance of ritual is reverent compliance with weighty rectitude; the date is auspicious and the canonical pattern is thus; We now dispatch [official] to conduct the welcome according to ritual."

sentences.zh: 答曰：“使者重宣中制，今日吉辰，備禮以迎。

translations.literal: The response read: "The envoy has again proclaimed the central edict; today is the auspicious day; all rites are prepared for the welcome.
translations.idiomatic: The response read: "The envoy has again proclaimed the central edict; today is the auspicious day, and all rites are prepared for the welcome.

sentences.zh: 螻蟻之族，猥承大禮，憂懼戰悸。

translations.literal: Our clan, mere ants, presumptuously receives this great ritual; anxious, fearful, trembling.
translations.idiomatic: Our clan, mere ants, presumptuously receives this great honor; I am anxious, fearful, and trembling.

sentences.zh: 欽率舊章，肅奉典制。”

translations.literal: Reverently following the old regulations, solemnly adhering to the canonical procedure."
translations.idiomatic: Reverently following the ancient regulations, I solemnly adhere to the canonical procedure."

sentences.zh: 餘如式。

translations.literal: The remainder follows the prescribed form.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder follows the prescribed form.

sentences.zh: 三月，禮部、太常寺上納後儀注：

translations.literal: In the third month, the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices submitted the protocol for taking the empress:
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices submitted the protocol for taking the empress:

sentences.zh: 發六禮制書。

translations.literal: Issuing the edicts for the Six Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The court issues the edicts for the Six Rites.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后御崇慶殿，內外命婦立班行禮畢，內給事出殿門，置六禮制書案上，出內東門。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager presided at the Chongqing Hall; inner and outer titled ladies formed ranks and completed their rites; the inner chamberlain exited the hall gate, placed the Six Rites edicts on the table, and exited the Inner Eastern Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager presided at the Chongqing Hall; titled ladies from within and without formed ranks and completed their rites; the inner chamberlain left the hall, set the Six Rites edicts on the table, and exited through the Inner Eastern Gate.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、通事舍人引由宣祐門至文德殿後門入，權置案於東上閣門。

translations.literal: Ritual officers and communication chamberlains led them through the Xuanyou Gate to enter by the rear gate of the Wende Hall, and temporarily placed the table at the Upper Eastern Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers and communication chamberlains led them through the Xuanyou Gate and in by the rear gate of the Wende Hall, temporarily setting the table at the Upper Eastern Gate.

sentences.zh: 命使納采、問名。

translations.literal: Appointing envoys to present gifts and inquire the name.
translations.idiomatic: The court appoints envoys to present gifts and inquire the name.

sentences.zh: 文德殿，宰臣、親王、執政官、宗室、百僚、大小使臣易朝服，樂備而不作。

translations.literal: At the Wende Hall, chief ministers, imperial princes, chief councillors, imperial clansmen, all officials, and great and minor envoys changed into court dress; music was prepared but not performed.
translations.idiomatic: At the Wende Hall, chief ministers, imperial princes, chief councillors, clansmen, all officials, and envoys great and small changed into court dress; music was prepared but not performed.

sentences.zh: 班定，內給事奉制書案置橫街北稍東，西向北上，禮直官、通事舍人引門下、中書侍郎，次引使、副就橫街南承制位，北向東上，內給事詣使者東，北面稱“太皇太后有制”，典儀曰“再拜”，在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: When ranks were set, the inner chamberlain, bearing the edict table, placed it slightly east on the north side of the cross street, facing west from the north; ritual officers and communication chamberlains led the Chancellery and Secretariat vice directors; next led the envoy and deputy to the place for receiving the edict on the south side of the cross street, facing north from the east; the inner chamberlain went to the envoy's east, faced north and announced "The Grand Empress Dowager has an edict"; the master of ceremonies said "Bow twice"; officials in attendance all bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: When the ranks were set, the inner chamberlain placed the edict table slightly east on the north side of the cross street, facing west from the north; ritual officers led the Chancellery and Secretariat vice directors, then the envoy and deputy to the edict-receiving station on the south side of the cross street, facing north from the east; the inner chamberlain stood to the envoy's east, faced north, and announced, "The Grand Empress Dowager has an edict"; the master of ceremonies called for a double bow, and all present officials bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 宣制曰：“皇帝納後，命公等持節行禮。”

translations.literal: The proclamation read: "The emperor is taking an empress; We command you to hold the staff of authority and perform the rites."
translations.idiomatic: The proclamation ran: "The emperor is taking an empress. We command you to bear the staff of authority and conduct the rites."

sentences.zh: 典儀曰“再拜”，使、副皆再拜。

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies said "Bow twice"; the envoy and deputy all bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies called for a double bow; the envoy and deputy both bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 授制書訖，典儀曰“再拜”，在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: When the edict had been handed over, the master of ceremonies said "Bow twice"; officials in attendance all bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict had been handed over, the master of ceremonies again called for a double bow, and all present officials bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 禮直官、通事舍人、太常博士引使、副從制案出，載於油絡網犢車，出宣德門，鼓吹備而不作。

translations.literal: Ritual officers, communication chamberlains, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians led the envoy and deputy, following the edict table out; it was loaded on an oil-net-covered calf cart; they exited the Xuande Gate; drums and pipes were prepared but not played.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers, communication chamberlains, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians led the envoy and deputy out with the edict table, loaded it on a net-covered calf cart, and exited the Xuande Gate; drums and pipes were prepared but not played.

sentences.zh: 至皇后行第大門外，令史二人對奉制案立，主人立大門內，儐者立主人之左，北面，進受命，出曰：“敢請事。”

translations.literal: Arriving outside the main gate of the empress's family residence, two clerks faced each other holding the edict table; the host stood inside the main gate; the usher stood to the host's left, facing north, advanced to receive the command, came out and said: "May I ask your business."
translations.idiomatic: At the main gate of the empress's family residence, two clerks faced each other holding the edict table; the host stood inside the gate; the usher stood to the host's left, faced north, advanced to receive the command, came out, and said, "May I ask your business."

sentences.zh: 使者曰：“某奉制納采。”

translations.literal: The envoy said: "I, [name], by imperial command present gifts."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "I, [name], by imperial command present gifts."

sentences.zh: 儐者入告，主人曰：“臣某之女若而人，既蒙制訪，臣某不敢辭。”

translations.literal: The usher entered to report; the host said: "My daughter [name] is as follows; having received the imperial inquiry, I, [name], dare not decline."
translations.idiomatic: The usher entered to report; the host said, "My daughter [name] is as described; having received the imperial inquiry, I, [name], dare not decline."

sentences.zh: 儐者出告，入引主人出大門外，再拜。

translations.literal: The usher came out to report, entered and led the host out beyond the main gate, and he bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The usher came out to report, then led the host out beyond the main gate, where he bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 使者先入，使者曰：“太皇太后制。”

translations.literal: The envoy entered first; the envoy said: "By edict of the Grand Empress Dowager."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy entered first and announced, "By edict of the Grand Empress Dowager."

sentences.zh: 主人再拜。

translations.literal: The host bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The host bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 宣制書畢，主人再拜受訖，主人進表訖，再拜，使者出。

translations.literal: When the edict had been proclaimed, the host bowed twice, received it, and finished; the host submitted his memorial and finished; bowed twice; the envoy departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict had been read, the host bowed twice and received it; he then submitted his memorial, bowed twice again, and the envoy departed.

sentences.zh: 問名同上儀。

translations.literal: Inquiring the name followed the same procedure.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiring the name followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 使者曰：“將加卜筮，奉制問名。”

translations.literal: The envoy said: "About to perform divination by tortoise and milfoil, by imperial command I inquire the name."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "About to perform divination by tortoise and milfoil, I inquire the name by imperial command."

sentences.zh: 主人曰：“臣某之女若而人，既蒙制命，臣某不敢辭。”

translations.literal: The host said: "My daughter [name] is as follows; having received the imperial command, I, [name], dare not decline."
translations.idiomatic: The host said, "My daughter [name] is as described; having received the imperial command, I, [name], dare not decline."

sentences.zh: 命使納吉、納成、告期並同命使納采、問名儀。

translations.literal: Appointing envoys to present auspicious omens, present the bride-price, and announce the date—all followed the same procedure as appointing envoys to present gifts and inquire the name.
translations.idiomatic: Appointing envoys to present auspicious omens, the bride-price, and announce the date all followed the same procedure as for presenting gifts and inquiring the name.

sentences.zh: 納吉，使者曰：“加請卜筮，占曰從制，使某納吉。”

translations.literal: For presenting auspicious omens, the envoy said: "Having additionally requested divination by tortoise and milfoil, the divination reads 'accord with the edict'; Envoy [name] presents auspicious omens."
translations.idiomatic: For presenting auspicious omens, the envoy said, "Having additionally requested divination by tortoise and milfoil, the divination reads 'accord with the edict'; Envoy [name] presents auspicious omens."

sentences.zh: 主人曰：“臣某之女若而人，龜筮雲吉，臣預有焉。

translations.literal: The host said: "My daughter [name] is as follows; the tortoise and milfoil say auspicious; your subject had anticipated this.
translations.idiomatic: The host said, "My daughter [name] is as described; the tortoise and milfoil pronounce auspicious; your subject had anticipated as much.

sentences.zh: 臣某謹奉典制。”

translations.literal: I, [name], reverently follow the canonical procedure."
translations.idiomatic: I, [name], reverently follow the canonical procedure."

sentences.zh: 告期，使者曰：“某奉制告期。”

translations.literal: Announcing the date; the envoy said: "Envoy [name], by imperial command, announces the date."
translations.idiomatic: For announcing the date, the envoy said, "Envoy [name], by imperial command, announces the date."

sentences.zh: 主人曰：“臣某謹奉典制。”

translations.literal: The host said: "Your subject [name] reverently follows the canonical procedure."
translations.idiomatic: The host replied, "Your subject [name] reverently follows the canonical procedure."

sentences.zh: 以上納吉、納成、告期。

translations.literal: The above covers presenting auspicious omens, presenting the bride-price, and announcing the date.
translations.idiomatic: The foregoing covers presenting auspicious omens, the bride-price, and announcing the date.

sentences.zh: 請見、授制、接表並如納采儀。

translations.literal: Requesting audience, conferring the edict, and receiving the memorial all followed the procedure for presenting gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Requesting audience, conferring the edict, and receiving the memorial all followed the gift-presenting ceremony.

sentences.zh: 臨軒命使冊後及奉迎於文德殿。

translations.literal: At imperial audience, envoys were appointed to invest the empress and conduct the welcome at the Wende Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At court, envoys were appointed to invest the empress and conduct the welcome at the Wende Hall.

sentences.zh: 百官朝服，皇帝常服乘輦至殿後閣，侍中奏中嚴外辦，乃服通天冠、絳紗袍，乘輦出自西房，降輦即御坐。

translations.literal: All officials in court dress; the emperor in ordinary dress rode the palanquin to the rear pavilion of the hall; the palace secretary reported inner strictness and outer readiness; then he donned the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, rode the palanquin out from the west chamber, descended, and took the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: All officials wore court dress. The emperor, in ordinary dress, rode the palanquin to the hall's rear pavilion. The palace secretary reported that inner strictness and outer readiness were complete; the emperor then donned the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, rode the palanquin out from the west chamber, descended, and took the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 兩省官及待制、權侍郎、觀察使以上，分東西入殿門，各就位，東西相向立。

translations.literal: Officials of the Two Departments and those of attendant draft status, acting vice ministers, and observation commissioners and above entered the hall gates east and west in separate groups, each took position, and stood facing each other east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Two Departments, attendant draft officials, acting vice ministers, and observation commissioners and above entered the hall gates in separate east and west groups, each took position, and stood facing one another.

sentences.zh: 奉寶置御坐前，奉宣後冊由東上閣門出，至文德殿庭橫行，典儀曰“拜”，在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: The seal was presented and placed before the imperial seat; the patent for the empress was carried out through the Upper East Gateway; arriving at the courtyard of the Wende Hall they proceeded crosswise; the ritual officer called "Bow," and all officials in position bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The seal was presented and placed before the imperial seat. The empress's patent was carried out through the Upper East Gateway to the Wende Hall courtyard, where the procession moved crosswise. The ritual officer called "Bow," and all officials in position bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 使、副受冊，宣制曰：“冊某氏為皇后，命公等持節展禮。”

translations.literal: The envoy and deputy received the patent; the edict was proclaimed: "We invest the [surname] clan as empress and command you to hold the staff of authority and carry out the rites."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy and deputy received the patent. The edict was proclaimed: "We invest the [surname] clan as empress and command you to hold the staff of authority and carry out the rites."

sentences.zh: 典儀曰“拜”，使、副再拜受冊寶訖，典儀讚百官再拜。

translations.literal: The ritual officer called "Bow"; the envoy and deputy bowed twice and received the patent and seal; when finished, the ritual officer prompted all officials to bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officer called "Bow." The envoy and deputy bowed twice and received the patent and seal. When finished, the ritual officer prompted all officials to bow twice.

sentences.zh: 宣制曰：“太皇太后制：命公等持節奉迎皇后。”

translations.literal: The edict was proclaimed: "By edict of the Grand Empress Dowager: We command you to hold the staff of authority and conduct the welcome of the empress."
translations.idiomatic: An edict was proclaimed: "By edict of the Grand Empress Dowager: We command you to hold the staff of authority and conduct the welcome of the empress."

sentences.zh: 典儀讚使、副再拜受節，又讚百官再拜。

translations.literal: The ritual officer prompted the envoy and deputy to bow twice and receive the staff; again prompted all officials to bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officer prompted the envoy and deputy to bow twice and receive the staff, then again prompted all officials to bow twice.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏禮畢解嚴，百官再拜出，皇帝常服還內。

translations.literal: The palace secretary reported that the rites were complete and strictness was lifted; all officials bowed twice and departed; the emperor in ordinary dress returned within.
translations.idiomatic: The palace secretary reported that the rites were complete and strictness was lifted. All officials bowed twice and departed, and the emperor, in ordinary dress, returned within.

sentences.zh: 冊寶至皇后行第，如納采儀。

translations.literal: When the patent and seal reached the empress's family residence, the procedure followed that for presenting gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When the patent and seal reached the empress's family residence, the ceremony followed that for presenting gifts.

sentences.zh: 使者曰：“某奉制授皇后備物典冊。”

translations.literal: The envoy said: "Envoy [name], by imperial command, presents the empress with the regalia of prepared goods and canonical documents."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "Envoy [name], by imperial command, presents the empress with the regalia of prepared goods and canonical documents."

sentences.zh: 皇后受冊寶，內外命婦序立如儀，主人以書奉使者。

translations.literal: The empress received the patent and seal; inner and outer appointed women took their positions in order according to ritual; the host presented a letter to the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The empress received the patent and seal. Inner and outer appointed women took their positions in order according to ritual, and the host presented a letter to the envoy.

sentences.zh: 奉迎。

translations.literal: Conducting the welcome.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony for conducting the welcome.

sentences.zh: 百官常服班宣德門外行第，儐者請，使者曰：“某奉制以禮奉迎。”

translations.literal: All officials in ordinary dress formed ranks outside the Xuande Gate at the family residence; the usher requested; the envoy said: "Envoy [name], by imperial command, conducts the welcome according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: All officials in ordinary dress formed ranks outside the Xuande Gate at the family residence. The usher requested entry, and the envoy said, "Envoy [name], by imperial command, conducts the welcome according to ritual."

sentences.zh: 儐者入告，主人曰：“臣某謹奉典制。”

translations.literal: The usher entered to report; the host said: "Your subject [name] reverently follows the canonical procedure."
translations.idiomatic: The usher entered to report. The host said, "Your subject [name] reverently follows the canonical procedure."

sentences.zh: 儐者出告，入引主人出大門外再拜。

translations.literal: The usher came out to report, entered, and led the host out beyond the great gate to bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The usher came out to report, reentered, and led the host out beyond the great gate to bow twice.

sentences.zh: 使者先入，曰“有制”，主人再拜，使者宣制畢，主人再拜受制，答表又再拜。

translations.literal: The envoy entered first, saying "There is an edict"; the host bowed twice; when the envoy had finished proclaiming the edict, the host bowed twice to receive the edict, responded with a memorial, and bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy entered first and announced, "There is an edict." The host bowed twice. When the envoy had finished proclaiming the edict, the host bowed twice to receive it, submitted a memorial in reply, and bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 姆導皇后，尚宅前引，升堂出立房外，典儀讚使、副再拜。

translations.literal: The instructress guided the empress; the Director of Palace Residences led before; they ascended the hall and came out to stand outside the chamber; the ritual officer prompted the envoy and deputy to bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The instructress guided the empress while the Director of Palace Residences led before. They ascended the hall and came out to stand outside the chamber, and the ritual officer prompted the envoy and deputy to bow twice.

sentences.zh: 使者曰：“今月吉日，某等承制以禮奉迎。”

translations.literal: The envoy said: "On this month's auspicious day, we, [names], by imperial command conduct the welcome according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "On this month's auspicious day, we, [names], by imperial command conduct the welcome according to ritual."

sentences.zh: 內侍受以入，使、副退，主人以書授使者，奉於司言，受以奏聞。

translations.literal: A palace attendant received it and entered; the envoy and deputy withdrew; the host presented a letter to the envoy, who delivered it to the Master of Announcements; it was received and submitted to report.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant received it and entered. The envoy and deputy withdrew. The host presented a letter to the envoy, who delivered it to the Master of Announcements; it was received and submitted in report.

sentences.zh: 皇后降立堂下再拜訖，升堂，主人升自東階，西向曰：“戒之戒之，夙夜無違命！”

translations.literal: The empress descended and stood below the hall to bow twice; when finished, she ascended the hall; the host ascended from the east steps, faced west, and said: "Be vigilant! Be vigilant! From early to late, do not disobey the command!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress descended and stood below the hall to bow twice. When finished, she ascended the hall. The host ascended from the east steps, faced west, and said, "Be vigilant! Be vigilant! From early to late, do not disobey the command!"

sentences.zh: 主人退，母進西階上東向，施衿、結帨曰：“勉之戒之，夙夜無違命！”

translations.literal: The host withdrew; the mother advanced up the west steps, faced east, adjusted the collar and tied the sash, and said: "Strive on! Be vigilant! From early to late, do not disobey the command!"
translations.idiomatic: The host withdrew. The mother advanced up the west steps, faced east, adjusted the collar and tied the sash, and said, "Strive on! Be vigilant! From early to late, do not disobey the command!"

sentences.zh: 皇后升輿至中門，升車出大門，使、副及群臣前引。

translations.literal: The empress mounted the sedan to the middle gate, mounted the carriage and exited the great gate; the envoy, deputy, and all ministers led before.
translations.idiomatic: The empress mounted the sedan to the middle gate, then mounted the carriage and exited the great gate, with the envoy, deputy, and all ministers leading before.

sentences.zh: 將至宣德門，百官、宗室班迎，再拜訖，分班。

translations.literal: As they were about to reach the Xuande Gate, all officials and imperial clansmen formed ranks to welcome; when they had bowed twice, they dispersed to their positions.
translations.idiomatic: As they approached the Xuande Gate, all officials and imperial clansmen formed ranks to welcome. After bowing twice, they dispersed to their positions.

sentences.zh: 皇后入門，鳴鍾鼓，班迎官退，乃降車入，次升輿入端禮門、文德殿、東上閣門，出文德殿後門，入至內東門內降輿，司輿前導，詣福寧殿門大次以俟。

translations.literal: The empress entered the gate; bells and drums sounded; the welcoming officials withdrew; she then descended from the carriage and entered; next mounted the sedan and entered through the Duanli Gate, the Wende Hall, and the Upper East Gateway; exited the rear gate of the Wende Hall; entered and at the Inner East Gate descended from the sedan; the Director of Sedans led before; they proceeded to the great side-chamber at the gate of the Funing Hall to wait.
translations.idiomatic: The empress entered the gate; bells and drums sounded, and the welcoming officials withdrew. She descended from the carriage and entered, then mounted the sedan and passed through the Duanli Gate, the Wende Hall, and the Upper East Gateway, exited the rear gate of the Wende Hall, and at the Inner East Gate descended from the sedan. The Director of Sedans led before as they proceeded to the great side-chamber at the Funing Hall gate to wait.

sentences.zh: 晡後，皇后車入宣德門，侍中版奏請中嚴，內侍轉奏，皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍，御福寧殿，尚宮引皇后出次，詣殿庭之東，西向立。

translations.literal: After mid-afternoon, the empress's carriage entered the Xuande Gate; the palace secretary submitted a memorial requesting inner strictness; a palace attendant relayed the report; the emperor donned the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe and presided at the Funing Hall; the Director of Palace Ladies led the empress out from the side-chamber to the east of the hall courtyard, where she stood facing west.
translations.idiomatic: After mid-afternoon, the empress's carriage entered the Xuande Gate. The palace secretary submitted a memorial requesting inner strictness, which a palace attendant relayed. The emperor donned the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe and presided at the Funing Hall. The Director of Palace Ladies led the empress from the side-chamber to the east of the hall courtyard, where she stood facing west.

sentences.zh: 尚儀跪奏外辦，請皇帝降坐禮迎，尚宮前引，詣庭中之西，東面揖皇后以入，導升西階入室，各就榻前立。

translations.literal: The Director of Ceremonies knelt and reported outer readiness, requesting that the emperor descend from his seat to welcome her with ritual courtesy; the Director of Palace Ladies led before; they proceeded to the west of the courtyard; the emperor faced east and bowed to the empress to lead her in; they were guided up the west steps into the chamber; each took position before the couch.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Ceremonies knelt and reported that outer preparations were complete, requesting that the emperor descend to welcome the empress with ritual courtesy. The Director of Palace Ladies led before to the west of the courtyard. The emperor faced east, bowed to the empress, and led her in. They were guided up the west steps into the chamber, where each took position before the couch.

sentences.zh: 尚食跪奏具，皇帝揖皇后皆坐，尚食進饌，食三飯，尚食進酒，受爵飲，尚食以饌從；

translations.literal: The Director of Food knelt and reported that all was ready; the emperor bowed to the empress and both sat; the Director of Food presented the meal; they ate three servings of rice; the Director of Food presented wine; they received the cup and drank; the Director of Food followed with the meal;
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Food knelt and reported that all was ready. The emperor bowed to the empress and both sat. The Director of Food presented the meal, and they ate three servings of rice. The Director of Food presented wine; they received the cup and drank, and the Director of Food followed with the meal;

sentences.zh: 再飲如初，三飲用巹如再飲。

translations.literal: The second round of drinking was as the first; the third round used the nuptial cup, as in the second round.
translations.idiomatic: The second round of drinking followed the first; the third round used the nuptial cup, as in the second.

sentences.zh: 尚儀跪奏禮畢，俱興，尚宮請皇帝御常服，尚寢請皇后釋禮服入幄。

translations.literal: The Director of Ceremonies knelt and reported that the rites were complete; both rose; the Director of Palace Ladies requested that the emperor put on ordinary dress; the Director of the Imperial Bedchamber requested that the empress remove her ceremonial dress and enter the curtained chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Ceremonies knelt and reported that the rites were complete. Both rose. The Director of Palace Ladies requested that the emperor put on ordinary dress, and the Director of the Imperial Bedchamber requested that the empress remove her ceremonial dress and enter the curtained chamber.

sentences.zh: 次日，以禮朝見太皇太后、皇太后，參皇太妃，如宮中之儀。

translations.literal: The next day, they paid ceremonial court visits to the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager and attended the Grand Imperial Consort, according to the palace procedure.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, they paid ceremonial court visits to the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager and attended the Grand Imperial Consort according to palace procedure.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 四月，太皇太后手書曰：“皇帝年長，中宮未建，曆選諸臣之家，以故侍衛親軍馬軍都虞候、贈太尉孟元孫女為皇后。”

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the Grand Empress Dowager wrote by hand: "The emperor has come of age, yet the Inner Palace has not been established; having selected from among the households of various ministers, We take the granddaughter of the late Commander-in-Chief of the Personal Guard Cavalry, posthumously enfeoffed Grand Marshal Meng Yuan, as empress."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, the Grand Empress Dowager wrote by hand: "The emperor has come of age, yet no empress has been installed. Having selected from among the households of various ministers, We take the granddaughter of the late Commander-in-Chief of the Personal Guard Cavalry, posthumously enfeoffed Grand Marshal Meng Yuan, as empress."

sentences.zh: 制詔：“六禮，尚書左仆射兼門下侍郎呂大防攝太尉，充奉迎使，同知樞密院事韓忠彥攝司徒副之；

translations.literal: An edict proclaimed: "For the Six Rites: Grand Secretary of the Left and concurrently Vice Director of the Department of the Chancellery Lü Dafang, acting as Grand Marshal, shall serve as welcome envoy; Privy Council Vice-Director Han Zhongyan, acting as Minister of Education, shall serve as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed: "For the Six Rites: Grand Secretary of the Left and concurrently Vice Director of the Department of the Chancellery Lü Dafang, acting as Grand Marshal, shall serve as welcome envoy, with Privy Council Vice-Director Han Zhongyan, acting as Minister of Education, as deputy;

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞蘇頌攝太尉，充發冊使，簽書樞密院事王岩叟攝司徒副之；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Left Secretariat Su Song, acting as Grand Marshal, shall serve as patent-issuing envoy; Privy Council Signatory Wang Yansou, acting as Minister of Education, shall serve as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Left Secretariat Su Song, acting as Grand Marshal, shall serve as patent-issuing envoy, with Privy Council Signatory Wang Yansou, acting as Minister of Education, as deputy;

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞蘇轍攝太尉，充告期使，皇叔祖、同知大宗正事宗景攝大宗正卿副之；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Left Secretariat Su Zhe, acting as Grand Marshal, shall serve as date-announcing envoy; the emperor's grand-uncle, Associate Director of the Imperial Clan Court Zong Jing, acting as Director of the Imperial Clan Court, shall serve as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Left Secretariat Su Zhe, acting as Grand Marshal, shall serve as date-announcing envoy, with the emperor's grand-uncle, Associate Director of the Imperial Clan Court Zong Jing, acting as Director of the Imperial Clan Court, as deputy;

sentences.zh: 皇伯祖、判大宗正事、高密郡王宗晟攝太尉，充納成使，翰林學士範百祿攝宗正卿副之；

translations.literal: The emperor's grand uncle, Director of the Imperial Clan Court and Prince of Gaomi Zong Sheng, acting as Grand Marshal, shall serve as bride-price envoy; Hanlin Academician Fan Bailu, acting as Director of the Imperial Clan Court, shall serve as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's grand uncle, Director of the Imperial Clan Court and Prince of Gaomi Zong Sheng, acting as Grand Marshal, shall serve as bride-price envoy, with Hanlin Academician Fan Bailu, acting as Director of the Imperial Clan Court, as deputy;

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王存攝太尉，充納吉使，權戶部尚書劉奉世攝宗正卿副之；

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Cun, acting as Grand Marshal, shall serve as auspicious-omens envoy; Acting Minister of Revenue Liu Fengshi, acting as Director of the Imperial Clan Court, shall serve as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Wang Cun, acting as Grand Marshal, shall serve as auspicious-omens envoy, with Acting Minister of Revenue Liu Fengshi, acting as Director of the Imperial Clan Court, as deputy;

sentences.zh: 翰林學士梁燾攝太尉，充納采、問名使，御史中丞鄭雍攝宗正卿副之。”

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Liang Tao, acting as Grand Marshal, shall serve as gift-presenting and name-inquiring envoy; Censor-in-Chief Zheng Yong, acting as Director of the Imperial Clan Court, shall serve as deputy."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Liang Tao, acting as Grand Marshal, shall serve as gift-presenting and name-inquiring envoy, with Censor-in-Chief Zheng Yong, acting as Director of the Imperial Clan Court, as deputy."

sentences.zh: 五月甲午，行納采、問名禮。

translations.literal: On jiawu of the fifth month, the rites of presenting gifts and inquiring the name were performed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu of the fifth month, the rites of presenting gifts and inquiring the name were carried out.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，行納吉、納成、告期禮。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the rites of presenting auspicious omens, presenting the bride-price, and announcing the date were performed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the rites of presenting auspicious omens, the bride-price, and announcing the date were carried out.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，帝御文德殿發冊及命使奉迎皇后。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the emperor presided at the Wende Hall to issue the patent and appoint envoys to conduct the welcome of the empress.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, the emperor presided at the Wende Hall to issue the patent and appoint envoys to conduct the empress's welcome.

sentences.zh: 己亥，百官表賀於東上閣門，次詣內東門賀太皇太后，又上箋賀皇后，上箋賀皇太妃。

translations.literal: On jihai, all officials submitted congratulatory memorials at the Upper East Gateway; next they proceeded to the Inner East Gate to congratulate the Grand Empress Dowager; they also submitted congratulatory documents to the empress and to the Grand Imperial Consort.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, all officials submitted congratulatory memorials at the Upper East Gateway, then proceeded to the Inner East Gate to congratulate the Grand Empress Dowager. They also submitted congratulatory documents to the empress and to the Grand Imperial Consort.

sentences.zh: 皇后擇日詣景靈宮行廟見禮。

translations.literal: The empress chose a day to proceed to the Jingling Palace to perform the temple-visitation rite.
translations.idiomatic: The empress chose a day to proceed to the Jingling Palace and perform the temple-visitation rite.

sentences.zh: 大觀四年，冊貴妃鄭氏為皇后，議禮局重定儀注：臨軒冊使，皇帝御文德殿，服通天冠、絳紗袍，百官朝服，陳黃麾細仗，依古用宮架。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daguan, when Imperial Consort Zheng was invested as empress, the Bureau for Deliberation on Ritual redrafted the ceremonial regulations: for the throne-hall patent envoy, the emperor would preside at the Wende Hall, wearing the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe; all officials in court dress; yellow banners and detailed guards would be arrayed; according to antiquity, the palace musical ensemble would be used.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daguan, when Imperial Consort Zheng was invested as empress, the Bureau for Deliberation on Ritual redrafted the ceremonial regulations. For the throne-hall patent envoy, the emperor would preside at the Wende Hall in the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe; all officials would wear court dress; yellow banners and detailed guards would be arrayed; and, according to antiquity, the palace musical ensemble would be used.

sentences.zh: 冊使出殿門，依近儀不乘輅。

translations.literal: The patent envoy exited the hall gate and, following recent practice, did not ride the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The patent envoy left through the hall gate and, per recent practice, did not ride the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 權以穆清殿為受冊殿。

translations.literal: The Muqing Hall was provisionally used as the patent-receiving hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Muqing Hall was temporarily designated as the hall for receiving the patent.

sentences.zh: 其日，皇后服禕衣，其奉冊寶授皇后，皆用內侍。

translations.literal: On that day, the empress wore ceremonial robes; presenting the patent and seal and conferring them upon the empress—all were performed by palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: On that day, the empress wore ceremonial robes, and presenting the patent and seal and conferring them upon her were all performed by palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 受冊訖，皇后上表謝皇帝，內外命婦立班稱賀，群臣入殿賀皇帝，於內東門上箋賀皇后。

translations.literal: When the patent had been received, the empress submitted a memorial thanking the emperor; inner and outer appointed women formed ranks to offer congratulations; the officials entered the hall to congratulate the emperor; at the Inner East Gate they submitted congratulatory documents to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the patent had been received, the empress submitted a memorial thanking the emperor. Inner and outer appointed women formed ranks to offer congratulations. Officials entered the hall to congratulate the emperor, and at the Inner East Gate submitted congratulatory documents to the empress.

sentences.zh: 其上禮儀注，乞依進馬條令施行；

translations.literal: As to the ceremonial regulations above, it was requested that they be implemented according to the regulations on presenting horses;
translations.idiomatic: Regarding the ceremonial regulations above, it was requested that they be implemented according to the regulations on presenting horses;

sentences.zh: 其會群臣，及皇后會外命婦儀注，並依《開元》、《開寶禮》。

translations.literal: the regulations for assembling the officials, and the empress's regulations for receiving outer appointed women, both followed the 《Kaiyuan Rites》 and the 《Kaibao Rites》.
translations.idiomatic: the regulations for assembling officials and for the empress's reception of outer appointed women both followed the 《Kaiyuan Rites》 and the 《Kaibao Rites》.

sentences.zh: 受冊之殿陳宮架，用女工，升降行止並以樂節，而別定樂名、樂章。

translations.literal: At the hall where the patent was received, the palace musical ensemble was arrayed; female musicians were used; ascending, descending, walking, and stopping were all regulated by music; separate music titles and hymn texts were established.
translations.idiomatic: At the hall where the patent was received, the palace musical ensemble was arrayed with female musicians; ascending, descending, walking, and stopping were all regulated by music, and separate music titles and hymn texts were established.

sentences.zh: 皇后上表乞免受冊排黃麾仗及乘重翟車、陳小駕鹵簿等，而於延福宮受冊。

translations.literal: The empress submitted a memorial requesting exemption from receiving the patent with yellow banners and guards, riding the heavy Di carriage, and displaying the lesser imperial guard of honor, and instead receiving the patent at the Yanfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress submitted a memorial requesting exemption from receiving the patent with yellow banners and guards, riding the heavy Di carriage, and displaying the lesser imperial guard of honor, asking instead to receive the patent at the Yanfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 其朝謁景靈宮，亦止依近例云。

translations.literal: Her court visit to the Jingling Palace likewise followed only recent precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Her audience at the Jingling Palace likewise followed only recent precedent.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年閏四月十七日，冊貴妃吳氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the intercalary fourth month of the thirteenth year of Shaoxing, Imperial Consort Wu was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day of the intercalary fourth month in the thirteenth year of Shaoxing, Imperial Consort Wu was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 前期，於文德殿內設東西房、東西閣，凡香案、宮架、冊寶幄次、舉麾位、押案位、權置冊寶褥位、受制承制宣制位、奉節位、讚者位、奉冊寶位、舉冊舉寶官位及文武百僚、應行事官、執事官位，皆儀鸞司、太常典儀分設之，以俟臨軒發冊。

translations.literal: In advance, within the Wende Hall east and west chambers and east and west pavilions were set up—incense tables, palace musical ensembles, patent-and-seal side-chambers, banner-raising positions, document-supervising positions, provisional positions for placing patent and seal cushions, positions for receiving edicts, proclaiming edicts, and announcing edicts, positions for presenting the staff, positions for the announcer, positions for presenting the patent and seal, positions for officials who lift the patent and seal, and positions for civil and military officials, participating officials, and officiating officials—all separately set up by the Directorate of Ceremonial and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices ritual officers, to await the throne-hall patent issue.
translations.idiomatic: In advance, within the Wende Hall's east and west chambers and east and west pavilions, incense tables, palace musical ensembles, patent-and-seal side-chambers, banner-raising positions, document-supervising positions, provisional positions for patent and seal cushions, positions for receiving, proclaiming, and announcing edicts, positions for presenting the staff, positions for the announcer, positions for presenting the patent and seal, positions for officials who lift the patent and seal, and positions for civil and military officials, participating officials, and officiating officials were all separately set up by the Directorate of Ceremonial and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices ritual officers, to await the throne-hall patent issue.

sentences.zh: 其日質明，皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍出西閣，協律郎舉麾奏《乾安之樂》，皇帝降輦即御坐，樂止，冊使、副以下應在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: At dawn on that day, the emperor, wearing the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, emerged from the west pavilion; the pitch-pipe officer raised the banner and the music 《Qi'an》 was played; the emperor descended from the palanquin and took the imperial seat; the music ceased; the patent envoy, deputy, and all officials who should be in position bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on that day, the emperor, wearing the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, emerged from the west pavilion. The pitch-pipe officer raised the banner and the music 《Qi'an》 was played. The emperor descended from the palanquin and took the imperial seat. The music ceased, and the patent envoy, deputy, and all officials who should be in position bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 侍中宣制曰：“冊貴妃吳氏為皇后，命公等持節展禮。”

translations.literal: The palace secretary proclaimed the edict: "We invest Imperial Consort Wu as empress and command you to hold the staff of authority and carry out the rites."
translations.idiomatic: The palace secretary read the edict: "We invest Imperial Consort Wu as empress and command you to hold the staff of authority and carry out the rites."

sentences.zh: 冊使、副再拜，參知政事以節授冊使，冊使跪受，以授掌節者。

translations.literal: The patent envoy and deputy bowed twice; the Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs conferred the staff on the patent envoy; the patent envoy knelt to receive it and passed it to the bearer of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: The patent envoy and deputy bowed twice. The Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs conferred the staff on the patent envoy, who knelt to receive it and passed it to the bearer of the staff.

sentences.zh: 中書令以冊授冊使，侍中以寶授副使，並權置於案，冊使、副以下應在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Director of the Department of State Affairs conferred the patent on the patent envoy; the palace secretary conferred the seal on the deputy envoy; both were provisionally placed on the table; the patent envoy, deputy, and all officials who should be in position bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Department of State Affairs conferred the patent on the patent envoy, and the palace secretary conferred the seal on the deputy envoy; both were provisionally placed on the table. The patent envoy, deputy, and all officials who should be in position bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 冊使押冊，副使押寶，持節者前導， 《正安之樂》作，出文德殿門，樂止，至穆清殿門外幄次，權置以俟。

translations.literal: The patent envoy carried the patent; the deputy envoy carried the seal; the bearer of the staff led before; the music 《Zheng'an》 was played; they exited the Wende Hall gate; the music ceased; at the side-chamber outside the Muqing Hall gate they were provisionally placed to wait.
translations.idiomatic: The patent envoy carried the patent and the deputy envoy carried the seal, with the bearer of the staff leading before. The music 《Zheng'an》 was played as they exited the Wende Hall gate. The music ceased, and at the side-chamber outside the Muqing Hall gate the patent and seal were provisionally placed to wait.

sentences.zh: 皇后首飾、禕衣出閣，協律郎舉麾，《坤安之樂》作，皇后至殿上中間南向立定，樂止。

translations.literal: The empress, in full head ornaments and ceremonial robes, emerged from the pavilion; the pitch-pipe officer raised the banner; the music 《Kun'an》 was played; the empress reached the center of the hall and stood facing south; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, in full head ornaments and ceremonial robes, emerged from the pavilion. The pitch-pipe officer raised the banner, the music 《Kun'an》 was played, and the empress reached the center of the hall and stood facing south. The music ceased.

sentences.zh: 冊使、副就內給事前東向跪稱：“冊使副姓某奉制授皇后備禮典冊。”

translations.literal: The patent envoy and deputy approached the inner provision director, knelt facing east, and announced: "The patent envoy and deputy, surnamed [name], by imperial command present the empress with the complete regalia of ceremonial patent and seal."
translations.idiomatic: The patent envoy and deputy approached the inner provision director, knelt facing east, and announced, "The patent envoy and deputy, surnamed [name], by imperial command present the empress with the complete regalia of ceremonial patent and seal."

sentences.zh: 內給事入詣皇后前，北向奏訖，冊使舉冊授內侍，內侍轉授內謁者監；
