translations.literal: The inner provision director entered and proceeded before the empress, faced north, and reported; when finished, the patent envoy raised the patent and conferred it on a palace attendant; the palace attendant passed it to the Director of Inner Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: The inner provision director entered and proceeded before the empress, faced north, and reported. When finished, the patent envoy raised the patent and conferred it on a palace attendant, who passed it to the Director of Inner Attendants;

sentences.zh: 副使舉寶授內侍，內侍轉授內謁者監；

translations.literal: the deputy envoy raised the seal and conferred it on a palace attendant; the palace attendant passed it to the Director of Inner Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: the deputy envoy raised the seal and conferred it on a palace attendant, who passed it to the Director of Inner Attendants;

sentences.zh: 掌節者以節授掌節內侍，內侍持節前導，冊寶並案進行入詣殿庭。

translations.literal: the bearer of the staff conferred the staff on the inner-attendant bearer of the staff; the palace attendant bearing the staff led before; the patent, seal, and table together advanced and entered the hall courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: the bearer of the staff conferred the staff on the inner-attendant bearer of the staff, who led before as the patent, seal, and table together advanced into the hall courtyard.

sentences.zh: 冊寶初入門，《宜安之樂》作，至位，樂止。

translations.literal: When the patent and seal first entered the gate, the music 《Yi'an》 was played; when they reached their positions, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: As the patent and seal first entered the gate, the music 《Yi'an》 was played; when they reached their positions, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 皇后降自東階，至庭中北向位，初行，《承安之樂》作，至位，樂止。

translations.literal: The empress descended from the east steps to the north-facing position in the courtyard; as she first walked, the music 《Cheng'an》 was played; when she reached her position, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress descended from the east steps to the north-facing position in the courtyard. As she began to walk, the music 《Cheng'an》 was played; when she reached her position, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 皇后再拜，舉冊官搢笏跪舉冊，讀冊官搢笏跪宣冊，內謁者監奉冊進授皇后，皇后受以授司言，又奉寶進授皇后，皇后受以授司寶。

translations.literal: The empress bowed twice; the official who lifts the patent tucked his tally and knelt to raise the patent; the official who reads the patent tucked his tally and knelt to proclaim the patent; the Director of Inner Attendants, bearing the patent, advanced and conferred it on the empress; the empress received it and passed it to the Master of Announcements; next the seal was borne forward and conferred on the empress; the empress received it and passed it to the Master of the Seal.
translations.idiomatic: The empress bowed twice. The official who lifts the patent tucked his tally and knelt to raise the patent; the official who reads the patent tucked his tally and knelt to proclaim it. The Director of Inner Attendants, bearing the patent, advanced and conferred it on the empress, who received it and passed it to the Master of Announcements. Next the seal was borne forward and conferred on the empress, who received it and passed it to the Master of the Seal.

sentences.zh: 司言、司寶置冊寶於案，舉冊寶官並舉案官俱搢笏舉冊寶並案興，詣東階之東，西向位置定。

translations.literal: The Master of Announcements and Master of the Seal placed the patent and seal on the table; the officials who lift the patent and seal and the officials who lift the table all tucked their tallies, raised the patent, seal, and table together, and stood; they proceeded to the east of the east steps, faced west, and took their positions.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Announcements and Master of the Seal placed the patent and seal on the table. The officials who lift the patent and seal and the officials who lift the table all tucked their tallies, raised the patent, seal, and table together, and stood. They proceeded to the east of the east steps, faced west, and took their positions.

sentences.zh: 皇后初受冊寶，《成安之樂》作，受訖，樂止。

translations.literal: When the empress first received the patent and seal, the music 《Cheng'an》 was played; when she had received them, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress first received the patent and seal, the music 《Cheng'an》 was played; once she had received them, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 皇后再拜，禮畢。

translations.literal: The empress bowed twice; the rites were complete.
translations.idiomatic: The empress bowed twice, and the rites were complete.

sentences.zh: 冊皇太子。

translations.literal: Investing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony for investing the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 至道元年八月壬辰，詔立皇太子，命有司草其冊禮，以翰林學士宋白為冊皇太子禮儀使。

translations.literal: On renchen of the eighth month of the first year of Zhidao, an edict installed the crown prince, ordered the responsible offices to draft the patent ceremony, and appointed Hanlin academician Song Bai as commissioner for the crown-prince patent ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen in the eighth month of Zhidao 1 (995), an edict installed the crown prince, ordered the responsible offices to draft the patent ceremony, and appointed Hanlin academician Song Bai commissioner for the crown-prince patent ceremony.

sentences.zh: 有司言：“前代太子無執圭之文，請如王公之制執桓圭，餘如舊制。”

translations.literal: The responsible offices reported: "In patent texts of former dynasties for crown princes there was no wording about holding a jade tablet; we request that he hold the Ring Scepter according to the rule for princes and dukes; the rest should follow the old regulation."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported: "Earlier patents for crown princes contained no wording about holding a jade tablet; we ask that the Ring Scepter be held as for princes and dukes, with the rest following the old regulations."

sentences.zh: 九月丁卯，太宗御朝元殿，陳列如元會儀，帝袞冕，設黃麾仗及宮縣之樂於庭，百官就位。

translations.literal: On dingmao of the ninth month, Taizong presided at the Chaoyuan Hall; the array followed the New Year's assembly procedure; the emperor wore robe and cap; yellow banners and guards and palace suspended music were set up in the courtyard; all officials took their positions.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao of the ninth month, Taizong presided at the Chaoyuan Hall. The array followed the New Year's assembly procedure. The emperor wore robe and cap; yellow banners and guards and palace suspended music were set up in the courtyard, and all officials took their positions.

sentences.zh: 太子常服乘馬，就朝元門外幄次，易遠遊冠、朱明衣，所司讚引三師、三少導從至殿庭位，再拜起居畢，分班立。

translations.literal: The crown prince in ordinary dress rode a horse to the side-chamber outside the Chaoyuan Gate; he changed into the yuanyou crown and vermilion bright robe; the officiants prompted and led the Three Preceptors and Three Minor Preceptors to escort him to his position in the hall courtyard; when they had bowed twice and inquired after his health, they dispersed to stand in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, in ordinary dress, rode a horse to the side-chamber outside the Chaoyuan Gate and changed into the yuanyou crown and vermilion bright robe. The officiants prompted and led the Three Preceptors and Three Minor Preceptors to escort him to his position in the hall courtyard. After bowing twice and inquiring after his health, they dispersed to stand in ranks.

sentences.zh: 太常博士引攝中書令就西階解劍、履，升殿詣御坐前，俯伏，興，奏宣制，降就劍、履位，由東階至太子位東，南向稱“有制”，太子再拜。

translations.literal: A Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician led the acting Director of the Department of State Affairs to the west steps to remove sword and shoes, ascend the hall, proceed before the imperial seat, prostrate, rise, report and proclaim the edict, descend to the sword-and-shoes position, and by the east steps reach the east of the crown prince's position; facing south, he announced "There is an edict"; the crown prince bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: A Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician led the acting Director of the Department of State Affairs to the west steps to remove sword and shoes, ascend the hall, proceed before the imperial seat, prostrate, rise, report and proclaim the edict, then descend to the sword-and-shoes position. By the east steps he reached the east of the crown prince's position, faced south, and announced, "There is an edict." The crown prince bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎引冊案就太子東，中書令北面跪讀冊畢，太子再拜受冊，以授右庶子；

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs led the patent table to the east of the crown prince; the Director of the Department of State Affairs, facing north, knelt and read the patent; when finished, the crown prince bowed twice and received the patent, passing it to the Right Subprefect;
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs led the patent table to the east of the crown prince. The Director of the Department of State Affairs, facing north, knelt and read the patent. When finished, the crown prince bowed twice and received the patent, passing it to the Right Subprefect;

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎進寶授中書令，中書令授太子，太子以授左庶子，各置於案。

translations.literal: the Vice Director of the Department of the Chancellery advanced with the seal and conferred it on the Director of the Department of State Affairs; the Director conferred it on the crown prince; the crown prince passed it to the Left Subprefect; each placed it on the table.
translations.idiomatic: the Vice Director of the Department of the Chancellery advanced with the seal and conferred it on the Director of the Department of State Affairs, who conferred it on the crown prince. The crown prince passed it to the Left Subprefect, and each placed it on the table.

sentences.zh: 由黃道出，太子隨案南行，樂奏 《正安之曲》，至殿門，樂止，太尉升殿稱賀，侍中宣制，答如儀。

translations.literal: They exited by the yellow path; the crown prince followed the table southward; the music played the 《Zheng'an》 melody; at the hall gate the music ceased; the Grand Marshal ascended the hall to offer congratulations; the palace secretary proclaimed the edict; the response followed the prescribed procedure.
translations.idiomatic: They exited by the yellow path, the crown prince following the table southward as the music played the 《Zheng'an》 melody. At the hall gate the music ceased. The Grand Marshal ascended the hall to offer congratulations; the palace secretary proclaimed the edict, and the response followed the prescribed procedure.

sentences.zh: 皇太子易服乘馬還宮，百官賜食於朝堂。

translations.literal: The crown prince changed clothes, mounted a horse, and returned to the palace; all officials were granted a meal in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince changed clothes, mounted a horse, and returned to the palace, and all officials were granted a meal in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 中書、門下、樞密院、師、保而下詣太子參賀，皆序立於宮門之外。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs, Department of the Chancellery, Privy Council, Preceptors, Protectors, and those below proceeded to the crown prince to pay their respects; all stood in order outside the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs, Department of the Chancellery, Privy Council, Preceptors, Protectors, and those below proceeded to the crown prince to pay their respects, all standing in order outside the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 庶子版奏外備，內臣褰簾，太子常服出次坐，中書、門下、文武百官、樞密、師、保、賓客而下再拜，並答拜；

translations.literal: The Subprefect submitted a memorial reporting outer readiness; inner attendants raised the curtain; the crown prince in ordinary dress emerged from the side-chamber and took his seat; the Department of State Affairs, Department of the Chancellery, civil and military officials, Privy Council, Preceptors, Protectors, Guests, and those below bowed twice, and he returned the bows;
translations.idiomatic: The Subprefect submitted a memorial reporting outer readiness. Inner attendants raised the curtain, and the crown prince, in ordinary dress, emerged from the side-chamber and took his seat. The Department of State Affairs, Department of the Chancellery, civil and military officials, Privy Council, Preceptors, Protectors, Guests, and those below bowed twice, and he returned the bows;

sentences.zh: 四品以下官參賀，升坐受之。

translations.literal: officials of the fourth rank and below paid their respects; he received them seated.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the fourth rank and below paid their respects, which he received seated.

sentences.zh: 越三日，具鹵簿，謁太廟，常服乘馬，出東華門升輅，儀仗內行事官乘車者，並服禮衣，餘皆袴褶乘馬導從。

translations.literal: Three days later, with full guard of honor, he visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple; in ordinary dress he mounted a horse, exited the Donghua Gate and mounted the imperial carriage; officiating officials within the guard who rode in carriages all wore ceremonial dress; the rest wore trousers and short jackets and rode horses in escort.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later, with full guard of honor, he visited the Imperial Ancestral Temple. In ordinary dress he mounted a horse, exited the Donghua Gate, and mounted the imperial carriage. Officiating officials within the guard who rode in carriages all wore ceremonial dress; the rest wore trousers and short jackets and rode horses in escort.

sentences.zh: 有司言：“唐禮，宮臣參賀皆舞蹈，開元始罷之。

translations.literal: The responsible officials reported: "In the Tang rites, when palace officials paid their respects they all performed the dance of obeisance; this was abolished beginning in the Kaiyuan period.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials reported: "Under the Tang rites, when palace officials paid their respects they all performed the dance of obeisance; this was abolished beginning in the Kaiyuan period.

sentences.zh: 故事，百官及東宮接見祗呼皇太子，上箋啟稱皇太子殿下，百官稱名，宮官稱臣；

translations.literal: By precedent, when all officials and the Eastern Palace received audiences they addressed only 'Imperial Crown Prince'; in memorials and reports they styled 'Imperial Crown Prince Your Highness'; officials of the bureaucracy used their personal names; palace officials styled themselves 'your subject';
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when all officials and the Eastern Palace received audiences they addressed only "Imperial Crown Prince"; in memorials and reports they styled "Imperial Crown Prince Your Highness"; officials of the bureaucracy used their personal names, while palace officials styled themselves "your subject";

sentences.zh: 常行用左春坊印，宮中行令。

translations.literal: for ordinary business the seal of the Left Spring Palace was used; orders were issued within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: for ordinary business the seal of the Left Spring Palace was used, and orders were issued within the palace.

sentences.zh: 又按唐制，凡東宮處分論事之書，太子並畫令，左、右庶子以下署名姓，宣奉行書按畫日；

translations.literal: Furthermore, according to Tang regulations, for all documents of the Eastern Palace disposing of affairs and deliberating matters, the crown prince would draw the command, and the Left and Right Subprefects and those below signed with surname; the promulgation and execution document followed the date of the drawing;
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, according to Tang regulations, for all Eastern Palace documents disposing of affairs and deliberating matters, the crown prince would draw the command, and the Left and Right Subprefects and those below signed with surname; the promulgation and execution document followed the date of the drawing;

sentences.zh: 其與親友、師傅，不用此制。

translations.literal: communications with relatives and friends and with teachers and tutors did not use this system.
translations.idiomatic: Communications with relatives, friends, teachers, and tutors did not use this system.

sentences.zh: 今請如開元之制，宮臣止稱臣，不行舞蹈之禮。

translations.literal: We now request that, following the Kaiyuan regulations, palace officials address themselves only as 'your subject' and not perform the dance of obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: We now request that, following the Kaiyuan regulations, palace officials address themselves only as "your subject" and not perform the dance of obeisance.

sentences.zh: 今皇太子兼判開封府，其所上表狀即署太子之位，其當申中書、樞密院狀，祗判官等署，餘斷案及處分公事並畫諾。”

translations.literal: The present crown prince concurrently serves as magistrate of Kaifeng Prefecture; the memorials and reports he submits bear the signature of the crown prince's position; for those that must be submitted to the Department of State Affairs and Privy Council, only the reviewing officials sign; all other case judgments and disposition of official business use the drawn approval."
translations.idiomatic: The present crown prince concurrently serves as magistrate of Kaifeng Prefecture. The memorials and reports he submits bear the signature of the crown prince's position. For those that must be submitted to the Department of State Affairs and Privy Council, only the reviewing officials sign; all other case judgments and disposition of official business use the drawn approval."

sentences.zh: 詔惟改‘諾’為‘準’，餘並從之。

translations.literal: The edict changed only 'approve' to 'authorized,' and approved all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: An edict changed only "approve" to "authorized" and approved all the rest.

sentences.zh: 其朝皇后儀，止用宮中常禮。

translations.literal: The procedure for court audiences with the empress used only the ordinary palace rites.
translations.idiomatic: The rite for court audiences with the empress followed only the ordinary palace procedure.

sentences.zh: 時真宗以壽王為皇太子，兼判開封，請見僚屬，稱名而免稱臣。

translations.literal: At that time Zhenzong, with Prince Shou as crown prince concurrently serving as magistrate of Kaifeng, when receiving audiences with his subordinates addressed them by personal name and exempted them from styling themselves 'your subject.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time, with Prince Shou as crown prince concurrently serving as magistrate of Kaifeng, Zhenzong, when receiving audiences with his subordinates, addressed them by personal name and exempted them from styling themselves "your subject."

sentences.zh: 神宗未及受冊禮而即位，乃以冊寶送天章閣，遂為故事。

translations.literal: Shenzong had not yet received the investiture rites when he ascended the throne; the patent and seal were therefore sent to the Hall of Heavenly Writings, and this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong had not yet received the investiture rites when he ascended the throne, so the patent and seal were sent to the Hall of Heavenly Writings instead, and this became precedent.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十二年五月，詔曰：“朕以不德，躬履艱難三十有六年，憂勞萬機，宵旰靡怠。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirty-second year of Shaoxing, an edict read: "We, lacking in virtue, have personally borne hardship for thirty-six years, troubled by the myriad affairs of state, never resting from early to late.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirty-second year of Shaoxing, an edict read: "We, lacking in virtue, have personally borne hardship for thirty-six years, troubled by the myriad affairs of state and never resting from early to late.

sentences.zh: 屬時多故，未能雍容釋負，退養壽康，今邊鄙粗寧，可遂如誌。

translations.literal: The times have been full of troubles; I have been unable to lay down my burdens with ease and retire to nurture longevity and health; now the frontier is roughly at peace, and I may fulfill my wish.
translations.idiomatic: The times have been troubled, and I have been unable to lay down my burdens with ease and retire in health; now the frontier is roughly at peace, and I may at last fulfill my wish.

sentences.zh: 皇子毓德允成，神器有讬，朕心庶幾可立為皇太子，仍改名，所司擇日備禮冊命。”

translations.literal: The prince has cultivated virtue and achieved completion; the sacred vessel has one to entrust it to; in my heart he may nearly be established as crown prince, and his name is also to be changed; the relevant offices shall select a day and prepare the ritual of investiture by patent."
translations.idiomatic: The prince has cultivated virtue to completion, and the throne has one worthy to receive it; I am minded to establish him as crown prince, change his name as well, and have the responsible offices choose a day and prepare the patent ceremony."

sentences.zh: 未及行禮，六月十一日內禪。

translations.literal: Before the ritual could be performed, on the eleventh day of the sixth month he abdicated within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before the ceremony could be performed, on the eleventh day of the sixth month he abdicated.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年八月十日，制立皇子鄧王愭為皇太子。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the eighth month of the first year of Qiandao, an edict established Prince Deng, Zhao Qi, as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the eighth month of the first year of Qiandao (1165), the court established Prince Deng, Zhao Qi, as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔以知樞密院洪適為禮儀使，撰冊文，簽書樞密院事葉顒書冊，工部侍郎王弗篆寶。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, an edict appointed Hong Shi, Director of the Privy Council, as master of ceremonies to draft the patent text; Ye Yong, Deputy Director of the Privy Council, to write the patent; and Wang Fu, Vice Minister of Works, to engrave the seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, the court appointed Hong Shi, Director of the Privy Council, as master of ceremonies to draft the patent; Ye Yong, Deputy Director of the Privy Council, to write it; and Wang Fu, Vice Minister of Works, to engrave the seal.

sentences.zh: 十六日，皇帝御大慶殿行冊禮，皇太子服遠遊冠、朱明衣，執桓圭。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day, the emperor presided at the Daqing Hall to perform the patent ceremony; the crown prince wore the Far-Traveling Cap and Vermilion Brightness Robes and held the Ring Scepter.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth day, the emperor presided at the Daqing Hall for the patent ceremony; the crown prince wore the Far-Traveling Cap and Vermilion Brightness Robes and held the Ring Scepter.

sentences.zh: 前期，習儀禮官及有司並先一日入宿衛，展宮架樂，設太子次、冊寶幄次、百官次，又設皇太子受冊位、典寶褥位，應行禮等皆有位，列黃麾半仗於殿門內外。

translations.literal: In advance, ritual officers practicing the ceremony and relevant offices all entered the guard quarters one day early; palace-frame music was set out; the crown prince's pavilion, patent-and-seal pavilion, and officials' pavilions were arranged; the crown prince's place for receiving the patent and the seal-display cushion were also set; all who were to perform rites had places; half a guard of yellow banners was posted inside and outside the hall gates.
translations.idiomatic: In advance, ritual officers rehearsing the ceremony and the relevant offices entered the guard quarters a day early; palace music was arranged; pavilions for the crown prince, the patent and seal, and all officials were set up; stations for receiving the patent and displaying the seal were prepared; every participant had an assigned place; and half a guard of yellow banners was posted at the hall gates.

sentences.zh: 質明，百官就次，皇太子常服詣幕次，符寶郎陳八寶於御位之左右，有司奉冊寶至幄次，百官朝服入班殿庭。

translations.literal: At dawn, all officials took their pavilions; the crown prince in regular dress went to his curtain pavilion; the Director of Seals and Treasures displayed the Eight Treasures to the left and right of the imperial seat; relevant offices brought the patent and seal to the pavilion; all officials in court dress entered ranks in the hall courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, all officials took their stations; the crown prince in regular dress went to his pavilion; the Director of Seals and Treasures displayed the Eight Treasures beside the imperial seat; the relevant offices brought the patent and seal to the pavilion; and all officials in court dress formed ranks in the hall courtyard.

sentences.zh: 有司自幄次奉冊寶至褥位，參知政事、中書令導從，退各就位，侍中升殿俟宣制，皇太子易服執圭俟於殿門外。

translations.literal: Relevant offices brought the patent and seal from the pavilion to the cushion; the Vice Director of the Secretariat and Secretariat Director guided them, withdrew, and each took his place; the Attendant-in-Chief ascended the hall to await the proclamation of the edict; the crown prince changed dress, took the scepter, and waited outside the hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices brought the patent and seal from the pavilion to the cushion, guided by the Vice Director and Director of the Secretariat, who then withdrew to their stations; the Attendant-in-Chief ascended the hall to await the edict; and the crown prince changed dress, took the scepter, and waited outside the hall gate.

sentences.zh: 樂正撞黃鍾之鍾，《乾安之樂》作，皇帝即御坐，殿上侍臣起居，樂止。

translations.literal: The chief musician struck the yellow bell; the music "Peace of Qian" was performed; the emperor took the imperial seat; attendants in the hall paid their respects; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The chief musician struck the yellow bell, and the "Peace of Qian" was performed; the emperor took his seat; attendants in the hall paid their respects; and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 行禮官讚引皇太子入就殿庭，東宮官從，初入殿門，《明安之樂》作，樂止，皇太子起居，次百官起居，各拜舞如儀。

translations.literal: Ritual officers announced and led the crown prince in to take his place in the hall courtyard, followed by Eastern Palace officials; upon first entering the hall gate, the music "Brightness of Ming" was performed; the music ceased; the crown prince paid his respects; next all officials paid their respects; each bowed and danced according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers announced and led the crown prince into the hall courtyard, followed by Eastern Palace officials; as he entered the hall gate, the "Brightness of Ming" was performed and then ceased; the crown prince paid his respects, then all officials did so, each bowing and dancing according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 皇太子詣受冊位，侍中前承旨，降階宣制曰：“冊鄧王愭為皇太子。”

translations.literal: The crown prince proceeded to the place for receiving the patent; the Attendant-in-Chief advanced to receive the order, descended the steps, and proclaimed the edict: "Invest Prince Deng, Zhao Qi, as crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince proceeded to his receiving station; the Attendant-in-Chief advanced to receive the order, descended the steps, and proclaimed: "Invest Prince Deng, Zhao Qi, as crown prince."

sentences.zh: 皇太子拜舞如儀，侍中升殿復位。

translations.literal: The crown prince bowed and danced according to ritual; the Attendant-in-Chief ascended the hall and returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince bowed and danced according to ritual; the Attendant-in-Chief ascended the hall and returned to his station.

sentences.zh: 中書令詣讀冊位，捧冊官奉冊至，中書令跪讀畢，興，皇太子再拜，有司奉冊至皇太子位，中書令跪以冊授皇太子，皇太子跪受，以授右庶子，置於案；

translations.literal: The Secretariat Director proceeded to the place for reading the patent; the patent-bearer brought the patent forward; the Secretariat Director knelt, read it through, and rose; the crown prince bowed twice; relevant offices brought the patent to the crown prince's place; the Secretariat Director knelt and handed the patent to the crown prince; the crown prince knelt to receive it and handed it to the Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household, who placed it on the table;
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Director went to the reading station; the patent-bearer brought the patent forward; the Director knelt, read it through, and rose; the crown prince bowed twice; the relevant offices brought the patent to his station; the Director knelt and handed it to the crown prince, who knelt to receive it and passed it to the Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household to set on the table;

sentences.zh: 次侍中以寶授皇太子，皇太子跪受，以授左庶子，如上儀。

translations.literal: Next the Attendant-in-Chief handed the seal to the crown prince; the crown prince knelt to receive it and handed it to the Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household, by the same procedure.
translations.idiomatic: next the Attendant-in-Chief handed the seal to the crown prince, who knelt to receive it and passed it to the Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household by the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 皇太子再拜。

translations.literal: The crown prince bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince performed a double bow.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人押冊、中允押寶以出，次皇太子出，如來儀。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Drafter escorted the patent and the Crown Prince's Household Supervisor escorted the seal as they exited; next the crown prince exited, as on entering.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Drafter escorted the patent out and the Crown Prince's Household Supervisor escorted the seal; then the crown prince departed by the same route he had entered.

sentences.zh: 初行樂作，出殿門樂止。

translations.literal: As they first set out, music was performed; upon exiting the hall gate, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Music played as they set out; it ceased when they passed through the hall gate.

sentences.zh: 次百官稱賀，樂正撞蕤賓之鍾，《乾安之樂》作，皇帝降坐，樂止，放仗，在位官再拜以出。

translations.literal: Next all officials offered congratulations; the chief musician struck the rui-bin bell; the music "Peace of Qian" was performed; the emperor descended from his seat; the music ceased; the guard was dismissed; officials in attendance bowed twice and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Next all officials offered congratulations; the chief musician struck the rui-bin bell and the "Peace of Qian" was performed; the emperor left his seat; the music ceased; the guard was dismissed; and all present officials bowed twice and departed.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，百官易常服，赴內東門司拜箋賀皇后，次赴德壽宮拜表箋賀，諸路監司、守臣等並奉表稱賀。

translations.literal: When the ritual was complete, all officials changed into regular dress, went to the Inner Eastern Gate office to present congratulatory documents to the empress, next went to the Deshou Palace to present congratulatory memorials and documents, and circuit supervisors, prefects, and the like all submitted memorials of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, all officials changed into regular dress, went to the Inner Eastern Gate to congratulate the empress, then to the Deshou Palace to congratulate the retired emperor; circuit supervisors, prefects, and other officials all submitted congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 明日，車駕詣德壽宮謝。

translations.literal: The next day, the imperial carriage proceeded to the Deshou Palace to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, the emperor went to the Deshou Palace to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 又明日，上御紫宸殿，引皇太子稱謝，還東宮，百官赴東宮參賀。

translations.literal: On the day after that, the emperor presided at the Zichen Hall, led the crown prince to offer thanks, returned to the Eastern Palace, and all officials went to the Eastern Palace to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day, the emperor presided at the Zichen Hall, led the crown prince to offer thanks, and sent him back to the Eastern Palace; all officials then went to the Eastern Palace to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 皇太子擇日先朝謁景靈宮，次日朝謁太廟、別廟，又擇日詣德壽宮稱謝。

translations.literal: The crown prince selected a day to first attend audience at the Jingling Palace; the next day attended audience at the Grand Ancestral Temple and subsidiary temples; and on another selected day proceeded to the Deshou Palace to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince chose a day to first pay court at the Jingling Palace; the next day he paid court at the Grand Ancestral Temple and subsidiary temples; and on another chosen day he went to the Deshou Palace to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 先是，禮官言：“皇太子朝謁景靈宮無所服典故，乞止用常服。

translations.literal: Earlier, ritual officers said: "For the crown prince's court audience at the Jingling Palace there is no precedent for dress; we request that only regular dress be used.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, ritual officers reported: "There is no precedent for what the crown prince should wear when paying court at the Jingling Palace; we ask that he wear only regular dress.

sentences.zh: 次朝謁太廟、別廟，當袞冕，乘金輅，設仗。”

translations.literal: For the next court audience at the Grand Ancestral Temple and subsidiary temples, he should wear the dark ceremonial robes, ride the golden carriage, and post a guard of honor."
translations.idiomatic: For paying court at the Grand Ancestral Temple and subsidiary temples, he should wear dark ceremonial robes, ride the golden carriage, and post a guard of honor."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted this.

sentences.zh: 皇太子言：“乘輅、設仗，雖有至道、天禧故事，非臣子所安。”

translations.literal: The crown prince said: "Riding the carriage and posting a guard of honor, although there are precedents from the Zhidao and Tianxi reigns, are not what a subject finds fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Riding the golden carriage and posting a guard of honor, though there are precedents from the Zhidao and Tianxi reigns, are not what a subject should accept."

sentences.zh: 詔免。

translations.literal: An edict exempted him.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted the exemption.

sentences.zh: 冊皇太子妃。

translations.literal: Investiture of the crown prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremony for investing the crown prince's consort.

sentences.zh: 政和五年三月，詔選皇太子妃。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year of Zhenghe, an edict ordered the selection of a crown prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year of Zhenghe (1115), the court ordered the selection of a crown prince's consort.

sentences.zh: 六年六月，詔選少傅、恩平郡王朱伯材女為皇太子妃，令所司備禮冊命。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year, an edict selected the daughter of Junior Tutor and Prince of Enping, Zhu Bocai, as crown prince's consort, and ordered the relevant offices to prepare the ritual of investiture by patent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year (1116), the court selected the daughter of Junior Tutor and Prince of Enping, Zhu Bocai, as crown prince's consort and ordered the responsible offices to prepare the patent ceremony.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，帝服通天冠、絳紗袍，御文德殿發冊。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, the emperor wore the Tongtian Cap and crimson gauze robe and presided at the Wende Hall to issue the patent.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengchen, the emperor wore the Tongtian Cap and crimson gauze robe and presided at the Wende Hall to issue the patent.

sentences.zh: 先是，議禮局上《五禮新儀》：“皇太子納妃，乘金輅親迎。”

translations.literal: Earlier, the Bureau for Discussing Rites submitted the New Rites of the Five Categories: "When the crown prince takes a consort, he rides the golden carriage to welcome her in person."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Bureau for Discussing Rites submitted the 《New Rites of the Five Categories》: "When the crown prince takes a consort, he should ride the golden carriage to welcome her in person."

sentences.zh: 皇太子三奏辭乘輅及臨軒冊命，詔免乘輅，而發冊如禮焉。

translations.literal: The crown prince three times memorialized declining the golden carriage and the patent ceremony at imperial audience; an edict exempted him from the golden carriage, but issuing the patent followed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince three times memorialized declining the golden carriage and the audience patent ceremony; the court exempted him from the carriage but issued the patent according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 公主受封，降制有冊命之文，多不行禮，惟以綸告進內。

translations.literal: When a princess received ennoblement, the issued edict contained language of investiture by patent, but for the most part the ritual was not performed; only an imperial silk announcement was submitted within.
translations.idiomatic: When a princess was ennobled, the edict often spoke of investiture by patent, but the formal ceremony was usually omitted; only an imperial silk announcement was submitted to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 至嘉祐二年，封福康公主為兗國公主，始備禮冊命。

translations.literal: By the second year of Jiayou, when Princess Fukang was ennobled as Princess of Yan, the full ritual of investiture by patent was first prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the second year of Jiayou (1057), when Princess Fukang was ennobled as Princess of Yan, was the full patent ceremony first performed.

sentences.zh: 前一日，百官班文德殿，內降冊印，宣制，冊案、援衛一如冊皇后儀。

translations.literal: On the previous day, all officials formed ranks at the Wende Hall; the patent and seal were brought down from within; the edict was proclaimed; the patent table and escorts followed the ceremony for investing the empress.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the ceremony, all officials formed ranks at the Wende Hall; the patent and seal were brought down from within and the edict proclaimed; the patent table and escorts followed the empress investiture ceremony.

sentences.zh: 有司先設冊使等幕次於內東門外，命婦次於公主本位門之外，公主受冊印位於本位庭階下北向，冊使位於內東門、副使及內給事於其南差退並東向，設冊印案位於冊使前南向，內給事位於冊使北南向。

translations.literal: Relevant offices first set pavilions for the patent envoy and others outside the Inner Eastern Gate; titled ladies' pavilions outside the gate of the princess's residence; the princess's place for receiving the patent and seal on the steps below her residence courtyard, facing north; the patent envoy's place at the Inner Eastern Gate; the deputy envoy and inner chamberlain south of it, somewhat withdrawn, all facing east; the patent-and-seal table south of and before the envoy; the inner chamberlain's place north of the envoy, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices first set pavilions for the patent envoy outside the Inner Eastern Gate; titled ladies' pavilions outside the princess's residence gate; the princess's receiving station on the steps below her courtyard, facing north; the envoy at the Inner Eastern Gate with the deputy and inner chamberlain to the south, slightly withdrawn, all facing east; the patent-and-seal table before the envoy, facing south; and the inner chamberlain north of the envoy, facing south.

sentences.zh: 自文德殿奉冊印將至內東門，內給事詣本位，請公主服首飾、褕翟。

translations.literal: From the time the patent and seal were borne from the Wende Hall until they reached the Inner Eastern Gate, the inner chamberlain went to the princess's residence and requested that the princess don her head ornaments and ceremonial robe.
translations.idiomatic: While the patent and seal were borne from the Wende Hall toward the Inner Eastern Gate, the inner chamberlain went to the princess's quarters and asked her to don her head ornaments and ceremonial robe.

sentences.zh: 冊印至內東門外褥位置訖，內臣引內命婦入就位，禮直官引冊使、副等俱就東向位，內給事就南向位。

translations.literal: When the patent and seal reached the cushion outside the Inner Eastern Gate and were set down, inner attendants led inner titled ladies in to take their places; ritual officers led the patent envoy, deputy, and others all to their east-facing places; the inner chamberlain took his south-facing place.
translations.idiomatic: When the patent and seal reached the cushion outside the Inner Eastern Gate, inner attendants led inner titled ladies to their stations; ritual officers led the envoy, deputy, and others to their east-facing stations; and the inner chamberlain took his south-facing station.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人、博士引冊使就內給事前東向，躬稱“冊使某、副使某奉制授公主冊印”，退復位，內給事入詣所設受冊印位公主前，言訖退。

translations.literal: Communication chamberlains and academicians led the patent envoy before the inner chamberlain, facing east; he bowed and announced "Patent Envoy [name] and Deputy Envoy [name], by imperial command, present the princess's patent and seal"; withdrew and returned to his place; the inner chamberlain entered, went before the princess at the place set for receiving the patent and seal, reported, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Communication chamberlains and academicians led the patent envoy before the inner chamberlain, facing east; he bowed and announced, "Patent Envoy [name] and Deputy Envoy [name], by imperial command, present the princess's patent and seal," then withdrew; the inner chamberlain entered, went before the princess at her receiving station, reported, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 內給事進詣冊使前西向，冊使跪以冊印授內給事，內給事跪授內謁者，內謁者及主當內臣等持入內東門，內給事從入詣本位，讚公主降詣庭中北向立，跪取冊，興，立公主右少前西向。

translations.literal: The inner chamberlain advanced to before the patent envoy, facing west; the patent envoy knelt and handed the patent and seal to the inner chamberlain; the inner chamberlain knelt and handed them to the inner chamberlain-supervisor; the supervisor and duty inner attendants carried them through the Inner Eastern Gate; the inner chamberlain followed in to the princess's residence; announced and led the princess down to stand in the courtyard facing north; knelt and took the patent; rose; and stood slightly before the princess's right, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The inner chamberlain advanced before the envoy, facing west; the envoy knelt and handed the patent and seal to him; he knelt and handed them to the inner chamberlain-supervisor; the supervisor and duty attendants carried them through the Inner Eastern Gate; the inner chamberlain followed to the princess's quarters, announced, and led the princess down to stand facing north in the courtyard; knelt and took the patent; rose; and stood slightly before her right, facing west.

sentences.zh: 又內給事立公主左少前東向，稱“有制”，讚者曰“拜”，公主再拜，右給事奉冊跪授之，公主受以授左給事，右給事又奉印授公主，如上儀。

translations.literal: Another inner chamberlain stood slightly before the princess's left, facing east, announced "There is an edict"; the announcer said "Bow"; the princess bowed twice; the right chamberlain, holding the patent, knelt and presented it; the princess received it and handed it to the left chamberlain; the right chamberlain again presented the seal to the princess, as above.
translations.idiomatic: Another inner chamberlain stood slightly before her left, facing east, announced, "There is an edict"; the announcer called for a bow; the princess bowed twice; the right chamberlain knelt and presented the patent, which the princess received and handed to the left chamberlain; the right chamberlain then presented the seal in the same way.

sentences.zh: 讚者曰“拜”，公主再拜畢，引公主升位。

translations.literal: The announcer said "Bow"; when the princess had finished bowing twice, they led the princess up to her seat.
translations.idiomatic: The announcer called for a bow; when the princess had bowed twice, they led her to her seat.

sentences.zh: 次內臣行內命婦賀畢，遂引公主謝皇帝、皇后，一如內中之儀。

translations.literal: Next inner attendants conducted congratulations from inner titled ladies; then led the princess to thank the emperor and empress, exactly as in inner-palace ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Next inner attendants conducted congratulations from inner titled ladies; then led the princess to thank the emperor and empress according to inner-palace ritual.

sentences.zh: 群臣進名賀。

translations.literal: All officials advanced in rank order to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The officials advanced in rank order to offer their congratulations.

sentences.zh: 其冊印如貴妃，有匣，文曰“兗國公主之印”。

translations.literal: Her patent and seal were like those of a noble consort, with a case; the inscription read "Seal of the Princess of Yan."
translations.idiomatic: Her patent and seal followed the noble consort's model, in a case inscribed "Seal of the Princess of Yan."

sentences.zh: 遂為定制。

translations.literal: This then became the fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This then became the established precedent.

sentences.zh: 神宗進封邠國大長公主、魯國公主皆請免冊禮，止進告入內云。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong advanced the titles of the Great Eldest Princess of Bin and the Princess of Lu, both requested exemption from the patent ceremony, submitting only an announcement to enter within.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong advanced the titles of the Great Eldest Princess of Bin and the Princess of Lu, both asked to be exempted from the patent ceremony and submitted only an announcement to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 冊命親王大臣之制，具《開寶通禮》，雖制書有備禮冊命之文，多上表辭免，而未嚐行。

translations.literal: The regulations for investing princes and great ministers by patent are fully set out in the Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao; although edicts contained language of preparing the ritual of investiture by patent, most submitted memorials declining, and it was never performed.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations for investing princes and great ministers by patent are fully set out in the 《Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao》; although edicts often spoke of preparing the patent ceremony, recipients usually memorialized to decline, and it was never actually performed.

sentences.zh: 每命親王、宰臣、使相、樞密使、西京留守、節度使，並翰林草制，夜中進入，翼日自內置於箱，黃門二人舁之，立御坐東。

translations.literal: Whenever princes, chief ministers, commissioners with seals, Privy Council directors, Western Capital custodians, or military commissioners were appointed, the Hanlin Academy drafted the text; it was submitted within at night; the next day it was placed in a box from within; two yellow-gate attendants carried it and stood east of the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever princes, chief ministers, commissioners with seals, Privy Council directors, Western Capital custodians, or military commissioners were appointed, the Hanlin Academy drafted the text overnight and submitted it within; the next day it was placed in a box, carried by two yellow-gate attendants, and set east of the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 內朝退，乃奉箱出殿門外，宣付閣門，降置於案，俟文德殿立班，閣門使引制案置於庭，宣付中書、門下，宰相跪受，復位，以授通事舍人，赴宣制位唱名訖，奉詣宰相，宰相受之，付所司。

translations.literal: When the inner audience concluded, they bore the box out beyond the hall gate, proclaimed and handed it to the Gate Department, lowered it onto the table, awaited the formation of ranks at the Wende Hall; the Gate Commissioner led the edict table and set it in the courtyard, proclaimed and handed it to the Secretariat and Chancellery; the chief minister knelt to receive it, returned to his place, and handed it to the communication chamberlain; he went to the edict-proclaiming place, called out the names; when finished, bore it to the chief minister; the chief minister received it and handed it to the relevant office.
translations.idiomatic: When the inner audience ended, they bore the box outside the hall gate, proclaimed it, and handed it to the Gate Department, which set it on a table; when ranks had formed at the Wende Hall, the Gate Commissioner led the edict table into the courtyard, proclaimed it, and handed it to the Secretariat and Chancellery; the chief minister knelt to receive it, returned to his place, and passed it to a communication chamberlain, who went to the proclamation station, called the names, then bore it to the chief minister, who received it and handed it to the relevant office.

sentences.zh: 若立後妃，封親王、公主，即先稱有制，百官再拜，宣制訖，復再拜舞蹈稱賀。

translations.literal: If establishing a consort or ennobling a prince or princess, they first announced "There is an edict"; all officials bowed twice; when the edict had been proclaimed, they again bowed twice, danced, and offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When establishing a consort or ennobling a prince or princess, they first announced, "There is an edict"; all officials bowed twice; when the proclamation was finished, they bowed again, danced, and offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 若宰相加恩制書，即宣付通事舍人，引宰相於宣制石東，北向再拜立，聽訖，拜舞復位。

translations.literal: If an edict conferring additional favor on the chief minister, it was proclaimed and handed to the communication chamberlain, who led the chief minister to the east of the edict stone, where he stood facing north, bowed twice, listened to the end, bowed and danced, and returned to his place.
translations.idiomatic: For an edict conferring additional favor on the chief minister, it was handed to a communication chamberlain, who led the chief minister to the east of the proclamation stone; he stood facing north, bowed twice, listened to the end, bowed and danced, and returned to his station.

sentences.zh: 若百官受制，即自班中引出聽麻，文班於宣制石東，武班於西，並如宰相儀，聽訖，出赴朝堂。

translations.literal: If all officials received an edict, they were led out from their ranks to hear the hemp announcement; the civil ranks east of the edict stone, the military ranks west, all following the chief minister's procedure; when finished, they went out to the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: When all officials received an edict, they were led from their ranks to hear the announcement; civil officials stood east of the proclamation stone and military officials west, all following the chief minister's procedure; when finished, they went to the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 其罷相者，即引出赴朝堂金吾仗舍。

translations.literal: Those dismissed as chief minister were led out to the Jinwu guard quarters of the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed chief ministers were led out to the Jinwu guard quarters of the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 諸王、宰相朝謝，前一日，內降官告，從內出東上閣門外宣詞以賜，授節者，仍交旌節。

translations.literal: When princes and chief ministers paid court to give thanks, on the previous day an appointment patent was brought down from within; it exited from within to outside the Upper Eastern Gate, where the text was proclaimed and bestowed; for those receiving staffs of authority, banners and staffs were also handed over.
translations.idiomatic: When princes and chief ministers paid court to give thanks, on the previous day an appointment patent was brought down from within, carried out through the Upper Eastern Gate, proclaimed, and bestowed; those receiving staffs of authority also received banners and staffs.

sentences.zh: 授者俯伏，執旌節交於頸上者三。

translations.literal: The recipient bowed prostrate and, holding the banner and staff, crossed them over the neck three times.
translations.idiomatic: The recipient bowed prostrate and, holding the banner and staff, crossed them over his neck three times.

sentences.zh: 參知政事、宣徽使、樞密使、大兩省、兩制、秘書監、上將軍、觀祭使以上授官告敕牒者，皆拜敕舞蹈，若止授敕或宣頭者止再拜，餘官悉不拜敕、不舞蹈，惟御史大夫、中丞拜授東上閣門使，又引至殿門外中籠門再拜。

translations.literal: Vice Directors of the Secretariat, Directors of the Palace Domestic Service, Privy Council directors, senior officials of both secretariats, drafters of both academies, Directors of the Palace Library, senior generals, commissioners of observation and sacrifice, and above who received appointment patents and commission documents all bowed to the edict and danced; if receiving only a commission or oral announcement, they bowed only twice; all other offices did not bow to the edict or dance; only the Censor-in-Chief and Vice Censor-in-Chief bowed to receive from the Upper Eastern Gate Commissioner, who also led them to the central cage gate outside the hall gate to bow twice again.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Directors of the Secretariat, Directors of the Palace Domestic Service, Privy Council directors, senior officials of both secretariats, drafters of both academies, the Director of the Palace Library, senior generals, and commissioners of observation and sacrifice and above who received appointment patents and commission documents all bowed to the edict and danced; those receiving only a commission or oral announcement bowed only twice; all other offices neither bowed to the edict nor danced; only the Censor-in-Chief and Vice Censor-in-Chief bowed to receive from the Upper Eastern Gate Commissioner, who also led them to the central cage gate outside the hall to bow twice again.

sentences.zh: 親王、節度、使相官告，並載以彩輿迎歸第。

translations.literal: Appointment patents for princes, military commissioners, and commissioners with seals were all loaded on colored carriages and welcomed back to their residences.
translations.idiomatic: Appointment patents for princes, military commissioners, and commissioners with seals were all carried on colored carriages in procession back to their residences.

sentences.zh: 親王輿中，設銀師子香合，輦官十二人，並襆頭、緋繡寬衣；

translations.literal: In the prince's carriage was set a silver lion incense box; twelve carriage attendants, all with kerchiefs and crimson embroidered wide robes;
translations.idiomatic: The prince's carriage held a silver lion incense box; twelve carriage attendants wore kerchiefs and crimson embroidered wide robes;

sentences.zh: 旌節各二，馬四，暴槊官十六人，執旌節攏馬對引，由乾元門西偏門出至門外；

translations.literal: two banners and staffs each, four horses, sixteen pike-bearing guards, holding banners and staffs and leading the horses in facing pairs, exiting through the western side gate of the Qianyuan Gate to outside the gate;
translations.idiomatic: two banners and staffs, four horses, and sixteen pike-bearing guards holding banners and staffs and leading the horses in facing pairs, exiting through the western side gate of the Qianyuan Gate;

sentences.zh: 馬技騎士五十人，槍牌步兵六十人，教坊樂工六十五人，及百戲、蹴鞠、鬥雞、角抵次第迎引，左右軍巡使具軍容前導至本宮。

translations.literal: fifty mounted trick-riders, sixty infantry with spears and shields, sixty-five musicians of the Music Bureau, and acrobatics, cuju, cockfighting, and wrestling in succession to welcome and lead; left and right military patrol commissioners with full military display going before as guides to the prince's residence.
translations.idiomatic: fifty mounted trick-riders, sixty infantry with spears and shields, sixty-five Music Bureau musicians, and acrobats, cuju players, cockfighters, and wrestlers in succession to welcome and lead; left and right military patrol commissioners with full military display escorting them to the prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 使相輿中用銀香爐，輦官十二人，金鵝帽、錦絡縫紫絁寬衣；

translations.literal: In the commissioner-with-seal's carriage was a silver incense burner; twelve carriage attendants with golden-goose caps and brocade-stitched purple silk wide robes;
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner-with-seal's carriage held a silver incense burner; twelve attendants wore golden-goose caps and brocade-stitched purple silk wide robes;

sentences.zh: 旌節各一，馬二，暴槊官八人，馬技騎士二十人，槍牌步兵二十四人，軍巡使不前導，餘如親王制。

translations.literal: one banner and staff each, two horses, eight pike-bearing guards, twenty mounted trick-riders, twenty-four infantry with spears and shields; military patrol commissioners did not go before as guides; the remainder followed the prince's regulations.
translations.idiomatic: one banner and staff, two horses, eight pike-bearing guards, twenty mounted trick-riders, and twenty-four infantry with spears and shields; military patrol commissioners did not go before as guides; otherwise the procession followed the prince's regulations.

sentences.zh: 有故則罷。

translations.literal: If there was a bereavement, it was canceled.
translations.idiomatic: The procession was canceled in the event of bereavement.

sentences.zh: 凡諫、舍、刺史以上在外任加恩者，悉令其親屬乘傳齎詔，就以告牒賜之。

translations.literal: For all remonstrance officials, drafters, prefects, and above receiving additional favor while serving outside the capital, their relatives were all ordered to travel by relay post bearing the edict and bestow the appointment notice on them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever remonstrance officials, drafters, prefects, and above received additional favor while serving outside the capital, their relatives were sent by relay post bearing the edict to bestow the appointment notice on them.

sentences.zh: 政和禮局上冊命親王、大臣儀，迄不果行。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe period the Rites Bureau submitted the ceremony for investing princes and great ministers by patent, but in the end it was never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe period the Rites Bureau submitted a ceremony for investing princes and great ministers by patent, but it was never carried out.
